11.s: sāntānikaṃ yakṣyamāṇamadhvagaṃ sārvavedasam guruarthaṃ pitṛmātryarthaṃ svādhyāyārthyupatāpinaḥ
11.d: सान्तानिकं यक्ष्यमाणमध्वगं सार्ववेदसम् गुरुअर्थं पितृमात्र्यर्थं स्वाध्यायार्थ्युपतापिनः
11.e: He who is seeking for progeny, he who is going to perform a sacrifice, a traveller on the road, he who has given away all his belongings, he who is begging for his preceptor, he who is begging for his parents, he who is begging for study, a sick man;—(1)—these nineBrāhmaṇas, who are religious mendicants, one should know as ‘Snātakas’; to these penniless men gifts shall be given, in proportion to their learning.

11.s: na vai tān snātakān vidyādbrāhmaṇān dharmabhikṣukān niḥsvebhyo deyametebhyo dānaṃ vidyāviśeṣataḥ
11.d: न वै तान् स्नातकान् विद्याद्ब्राह्मणान् धर्मभिक्षुकान् निःस्वेभ्यो देयमेतेभ्यो दानं विद्याविशेषतः
11.e: He who is seeking for progeny, he who is going to perform a sacrifice, a traveller on the road, he who has given away all his belongings, he who is begging for his preceptor, he who is begging for his parents, he who is begging for study, a sick man;—(1)—these nineBrāhmaṇas, who are religious mendicants, one should know as ‘Snātakas’; to these penniless men gifts shall be given, in proportion to their learning.

11.s: etebhyo hi dvijāgryebhyo deyamannaṃ sadakṣiṇam itarebhyo bahirvedi kṛtānnaṃ deyamucyate
11.d: एतेभ्यो हि द्विजाग्र्येभ्यो देयमन्नं सदक्षिणम् इतरेभ्यो बहिर्वेदि कृतान्नं देयमुच्यते
11.e: For these best of twice-born men, the ‘gift’ shall consist of food accompanied by a present; for others, ‘gift’ has been declared to be the cooked food given outside the sacrificial enclosure.

11.s: sarvaratnāni rājā tu yathārhaṃ pratipādayet brāhmaṇān vedaviduṣo yajñārthaṃ caiva dakṣiṇām
11.d: सर्वरत्नानि राजा तु यथार्हं प्रतिपादयेत् ब्राह्मणान् वेदविदुषो यज्ञार्थं चैव दक्षिणाम्
11.e: OnBrāhmaṇaslearned in the veda, the king shall bestow, according to their desert, all kinds of jewels, as also presents for sacrificial performances.

11.s: kṛtadāro 'parān dārān bhikṣitvā yo 'dhigacchati ratimātraṃ phalaṃ tasya dravyadātustu saṃtatiḥ
11.d: कृतदारो ऽपरान् दारान् भिक्षित्वा यो ऽधिगच्छति रतिमात्रं फलं तस्य द्रव्यदातुस्तु संततिः
11.e: If a man, having already got a wife, weds another wife, after having begged (for the requisite wealth), sexual enjoyment is his only fruit; the issue belongs to the person who gave him the wealth.

11.s: dhanāni tu yathāśakti vipreṣu pratipādayet vedavitsu vivikteṣu pretya svargaṃ samaśnute
11.d: धनानि तु यथाशक्ति विप्रेषु प्रतिपादयेत् वेदवित्सु विविक्तेषु प्रेत्य स्वर्गं समश्नुते
11.e: One should give, according to one’s ability, wealth to Brāhmaṇas learned in the Veda and living alone; (thus) one obtains after death heavenly bliss..

11.s: yasya traivārṣikaṃ bhaktaṃ paryāptaṃ bhṛtyavṛttaye adhikaṃ vā 'pi vidyeta sa somaṃ pātumarhati
11.d: यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यवृत्तये अधिकं वा ऽपि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति
11.e: For this reason, if a twice-born person possessing less wealth drinks Soma, he does not obtain its reward, even though he may have drunk Soma formerly.

11.s: ataḥ svalpīyasi dravye yaḥ somaṃ pibati dvijaḥ sa pītasomapūrvo 'pi na tasyāpnoti tatphalam
11.d: अतः स्वल्पीयसि द्रव्ये यः सोमं पिबति द्विजः स पीतसोमपूर्वो ऽपि न तस्याप्नोति तत्फलम्
11.e: If a wealthy man gives to other people, while his own people are living in distress,—such counterfeit virtue would be like swallowing poison, which is sweet in the beginning.

11.s: śaktaḥ parajane dātā svajane duḥkhajīvini madhvāpāto viṣāsvādaḥ sa dharmapratirūpakaḥ
11.d: शक्तः परजने दाता स्वजने दुःखजीविनि मध्वापातो विषास्वादः स धर्मप्रतिरूपकः
11.e: If a man does anything for his own benefit after death, to the detriment of the persons he has got to maintain,—it becomes conducive to unhappy results while he lives as also when he dies.—(9). Aged parents, well-behaved wife and infant sons have been declared by Manu to be persons that should be maintained, even by doing a hundred evil acts.

11.s: bhṛtyānāmuparodhena yat karotyaurdhvadehikam tadbhavatyasukhaudarkaṃ jīvataśca mṛtasya ca
11.d: भृत्यानामुपरोधेन यत् करोत्यौर्ध्वदेहिकम् तद्भवत्यसुखौदर्कं जीवतश्च मृतस्य च
11.e: If a man does anything for his own benefit after death, to the detriment of the persons he has got to maintain,—it becomes conducive to unhappy results while he lives as also when he dies.—(9). Aged parents, well-behaved wife and infant sons have been declared by Manu to be persons that should be maintained, even by doing a hundred evil acts.

11.s: yajñaścet pratiruddhaḥ syādekenāṅgena yajvanaḥ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣena dhārmike sati rājani
11.d: यज्ञश्चेत् प्रतिरुद्धः स्यादेकेनाङ्गेन यज्वनः ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेन धार्मिके सति राजनि
11.e: During the reign of a righteous king, if the sacrificial rite of a sacrificer, specially of aBrāhmaṇa, be interrupted for want of one requisite,—that substance may be appropriated, for the completion of that sacrifice, from the house of a Vaiśya possessed of many cattle, who does not perform sacrifices and does not drink the Soma.

11.s: yo vaiśyaḥ syādbahupaśurhīnakraturasomapaḥ kuṭumbāt tasya taddravyamāharedyajñasiddhaye
11.d: यो वैश्यः स्याद्बहुपशुर्हीनक्रतुरसोमपः कुटुम्बात् तस्य तद्द्रव्यमाहरेद्यज्ञसिद्धये
11.e: During the reign of a righteous king, if the sacrificial rite of a sacrificer, specially of aBrāhmaṇa, be interrupted for want of one requisite,—that substance may be appropriated, for the completion of that sacrifice, from the house of a Vaiśya possessed of many cattle, who does not perform sacrifices and does not drink the Soma.

11.s: āharet trīṇi vā dve vā kāmaṃ śūdrasya veśmanaḥ na hi śūdrasya yajñeṣu kaścidasti parigrahaḥ
11.d: आहरेत् त्रीणि वा द्वे वा कामं शूद्रस्य वेश्मनः न हि शूद्रस्य यज्ञेषु कश्चिदस्ति परिग्रहः
11.e: Or, he may freely take away two or three things from the house of aŚūdra; for theŚūdrahas nothing to do with acrifices.

11.s: yo 'nāhitāgniḥ śatagurayajvā ca sahasraguḥ ayajñaś tayorapi kuṭumbābhyāmāharedavicārayan
11.d: यो ऽनाहिताग्निः शतगुरयज्वा च सहस्रगुः अयज्ञश् तयोरपि कुटुम्बाभ्यामाहरेदविचारयन्
11.e: If a man, possessing a hundred cows, has not laid the Fire,—or a man possessing a thousand cows, performs no sacrifices,—out of the houses of these men also, one may take away (the sacrificial requisites) without hesitation.

11.s: ādānanityāccādāturāharedaprayacchataḥ tathā yaśo 'sya prathate dharmaścaiva pravardhate
11.d: आदाननित्याच्चादातुराहरेदप्रयच्छतः तथा यशो ऽस्य प्रथते धर्मश्चैव प्रवर्धते
11.e: He shall take it also from one who always acquires, and never gives, if he refuses to give up the thing; thus does his fame spread and merit increase.

11.s: tathā 'iva saptame bhakte bhaktāni ṣaḍanaśnatā aśvastanavidhānena hartavyaṃ hīnakarmaṇaḥ
11.d: तथा ऽइव सप्तमे भक्ते भक्तानि षडनश्नता अश्वस्तनविधानेन हर्तव्यं हीनकर्मणः
11.e: Likewise one who has not eaten six meals, may, for the seventh meal, take from a person whose sacred duties are neglected,—but only to this extent that it does not last till the morrow;—(16) either from the threshing yard, or from the field, or from the house, or from any place where it may be got; but if the owner questions him, he must confess it to the questioner.

11.s: khalāt kṣetrādagārādvā yato vā 'pyupalabhyate ākhyātavyaṃ tu tat tasmai pṛcchate yadi pṛcchati
11.d: खलात् क्षेत्रादगाराद्वा यतो वा ऽप्युपलभ्यते आख्यातव्यं तु तत् तस्मै पृच्छते यदि पृच्छति
11.e: Likewise one who has not eaten six meals, may, for the seventh meal, take from a person whose sacred duties are neglected,—but only to this extent that it does not last till the morrow;—(16) either from the threshing yard, or from the field, or from the house, or from any place where it may be got; but if the owner questions him, he must confess it to the questioner.

11.s: brāhmaṇasvaṃ na hartavyaṃ kṣatriyeṇa kadā cana dasyuniṣkriyayostu svamajīvan hartumarhati
11.d: ब्राह्मणस्वं न हर्तव्यं क्षत्रियेण कदा चन दस्युनिष्क्रिययोस्तु स्वमजीवन् हर्तुमर्हति
11.e: TheKṣatriyashall never appropriate the property of aBrāhmaṇa; when starving, he may appropriate the property of the robbers and of one who neglects his duties.

11.s: yo 'sādhubhyo 'rthamādāya sādhubhyaḥ saṃprayacchati sa kṛtvā plavamātmānaṃ saṃtārayati tāvubhau
11.d: यो ऽसाधुभ्यो ऽर्थमादाय साधुभ्यः संप्रयच्छति स कृत्वा प्लवमात्मानं संतारयति तावुभौ
11.e: He who takes wealth from the wicked and gives it to the virtuous, makes himself a raft and carries both over.

11.s: yaddhanaṃ yajñaśīlānāṃ devasvaṃ tadvidurbudhāḥ ayajvanāṃ tu yadvittamāsurasvaṃ taducyate
11.d: यद्धनं यज्ञशीलानां देवस्वं तद्विदुर्बुधाः अयज्वनां तु यद्वित्तमासुरस्वं तदुच्यते
11.e: The property of persons given to perform sacrifices the learned regard as ‘the property of the gods;’ while the property of those who do not perform sacrifices is described as ‘the property of demons.’

11.s: na tasmin dhārayeddaṇḍaṃ dhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ kṣatriyasya hi bāliśyādbrāhmaṇaḥ sīdati kṣudhā
11.d: न तस्मिन् धारयेद्दण्डं धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः क्षत्रियस्य हि बालिश्याद्ब्राह्मणः सीदति क्षुधा
11.e: The righteous king shall inflict no punishment upon him; as it is only through the foolishness of theKṣatriyathat theBrāhmaṇasuffers from hunger.

11.s: tasya bhṛtyajanaṃ jñātvā svakuṭumbān mahīpatiḥ śrutaśīle ca vijñāya vṛttiṃ dharmyāṃ prakalpayet
11.d: तस्य भृत्यजनं ज्ञात्वा स्वकुटुम्बान् महीपतिः श्रुतशीले च विज्ञाय वृत्तिं धर्म्यां प्रकल्पयेत्
11.e: Having ascertained the number of persons he has to maintain, and having investigated his learning and character, the king shall provide, out of his own property, a proper living for him.

11.s: kalpayitvā 'sya vṛttiṃ ca rakṣedenaṃ samantataḥ rājā hi dharmaṣaḍbhāgaṃ tasmāt prāpnoti rakṣitāt
11.d: कल्पयित्वा ऽस्य वृत्तिं च रक्षेदेनं समन्ततः राजा हि धर्मषड्भागं तस्मात् प्राप्नोति रक्षितात्
11.e: Having provided a living for him, the king shall protect him in every way; since he obtains, from the person thus protected, the sixth part of his spiritual merit.

11.s: na yajñārthaṃ dhanaṃ śūdrādvipro bhikṣeta karhi cit yajamāno hi bhikṣitvā caṇḍālaḥ pretya jāyate
11.d: न यज्ञार्थं धनं शूद्राद्विप्रो भिक्षेत कर्हि चित् यजमानो हि भिक्षित्वा चण्डालः प्रेत्य जायते
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇashall never beg from aŚūdrawealth for the purpose of sacrificial performances; if one perform sacrifices with wealth so begged, he is born, after death, as aCaṇḍāla.

11.s: yājñārthamarthaṃ bhikṣitvā yo na sarvaṃ prayacchati sa yāti bhāsatāṃ vipraḥ kākatāṃ vā śataṃ samāḥ
11.d: याज्ञार्थमर्थं भिक्षित्वा यो न सर्वं प्रयच्छति स याति भासतां विप्रः काकतां वा शतं समाः
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇa, having begged wealth for a sacrifice, does not spend the whole of it, he becomes, for a hundred years, aBhāsaor acrow.

11.s: devasvaṃ brāhmaṇasvaṃ vā lobhenaupahinasti yaḥ sa pāpātmā pare loke gṛdhraucchiṣṭena jīvati
11.d: देवस्वं ब्राह्मणस्वं वा लोभेनौपहिनस्ति यः स पापात्मा परे लोके गृध्रौच्छिष्टेन जीवति
11.e: The sinful man who, through covetousness, seizes the property of the gods, or the property ofBrāhmaṇas, lives, in the other world, upon the leavings of vultures.

11.s: iṣṭiṃ vaiśvānarīṃ nityaṃ nirvapedabdaparyaye kḷptānāṃ paśusomānāṃ niṣkṛtyarthamasaṃbhave
11.d: इष्टिं वैश्वानरीं नित्यं निर्वपेदब्दपर्यये कॢप्तानां पशुसोमानां निष्कृत्यर्थमसंभवे
11.e: In the event of the impossibility of the performance of the prescribed Animal and Soma sacrifices, one shall always offer theVaiśvānarīsacrifice at the change of the year,—in expiation thereof.

11.s: āpatkalpena yo dharmaṃ kurute 'nāpadi dvijaḥ sa nāpnoti phalaṃ tasya paratraiti vicāritam
11.d: आपत्कल्पेन यो धर्मं कुरुते ऽनापदि द्विजः स नाप्नोति फलं तस्य परत्रैति विचारितम्
11.e: If a twice-born person performs, even in normal times, a sacred act according to the mode sanctioned for Abnormal Times,—he does not obtain its reward. Such is the well-considered opinion.

11.s: viśvaiśca devaiḥ sādhyaiśca brāhmaṇaiśca maharṣibhiḥ āpatsu maraṇādbhītairvidheḥ pratinidhiḥ kṛtaḥ
11.d: विश्वैश्च देवैः साध्यैश्च ब्राह्मणैश्च महर्षिभिः आपत्सु मरणाद्भीतैर्विधेः प्रतिनिधिः कृतः
11.e: The substitute of the Primary Rule was ordained by theViśvedevas, theSādhyasand the greatBrāhmaṇaSages, when they were afraid of perishing in abnormal times.

11.s: prabhuḥ prathamakalpasya yo 'nukalpena vartate na sāṃparāyikaṃ tasya durmatervidyate phalam
11.d: प्रभुः प्रथमकल्पस्य यो ऽनुकल्पेन वर्तते न सांपरायिकं तस्य दुर्मतेर्विद्यते फलम्
11.e: If one, who is able to fulfil the primary rule, adopts the substitute,—this evil-minded man does not obtain its reward in the other world.

11.s: na brāhmaṇo vedayeta kiṃ cidrājani dharmavit svavīryeṇaiva tāṃśiṣyān mānavānapakāriṇaḥ
11.d: न ब्राह्मणो वेदयेत किं चिद्राजनि धर्मवित् स्ववीर्येणैव तांशिष्यान् मानवानपकारिणः
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇaconversant with the Law shall not complain to the King; by his own power alone he shall punish the men that injure him.

11.s: svavīryādrājavīryācca svavīryaṃ balavattaram tasmāt svenaiva vīryeṇa nigṛhṇīyādarīn dvijaḥ
11.d: स्ववीर्याद्राजवीर्याच्च स्ववीर्यं बलवत्तरम् तस्मात् स्वेनैव वीर्येण निगृह्णीयादरीन् द्विजः
11.e: His own power is more forcible than the King’s power; the twice-born man shall, therefore, punish his enemies by his own power.

11.s: śrutīratharvāṅgirasīḥ kuryādityavicārayan vākṣastraṃ vai brāhmaṇasya tena hanyādarīn dvijaḥ
11.d: श्रुतीरथर्वाङ्गिरसीः कुर्यादित्यविचारयन् वाक्षस्त्रं वै ब्राह्मणस्य तेन हन्यादरीन् द्विजः
11.e: He should make use of the sacred texts of the Atharva-Veda, without hesitation. Speech indeed is theBrāhmaṇa’sweapon; by that should the twice-born strike his enemies.

11.s: kṣatriyo bāhuvīryeṇa taredāpadamātmanaḥ dhanena vaiśyaśūdrau tu japahomairdvijottamaḥ
11.d: क्षत्रियो बाहुवीर्येण तरेदापदमात्मनः धनेन वैश्यशूद्रौ तु जपहोमैर्द्विजोत्तमः
11.e: TheKṣatriyashall cut through his misfortunes by the strength of his arms; the Vaiśya and theŚūdraby their wealth, and the chief of the twice-born by muttered prayers and oblations into the fire.

11.s: vidhātā śāsitā vaktā maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate tasmai nākuśalaṃ brūyānna śuṣkāṃ giramīrayet
11.d: विधाता शासिता वक्ता मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते तस्मै नाकुशलं ब्रूयान्न शुष्कां गिरमीरयेत्
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇais called the creator, the punisher, the teacher and the advisor; therefore one should not address unpleasant words to him, nor use any harsh words.

11.s: na vai kanyā na yuvatirnālpavidyo na bāliśaḥ hotā syādagnihotrasya nārto nāsaṃskṛtastathā
11.d: न वै कन्या न युवतिर्नाल्पविद्यो न बालिशः होता स्यादग्निहोत्रस्य नार्तो नासंस्कृतस्तथा
11.e: Neither a girl, nor a youthful woman, nor a man of little learning, nor a fool, nor one distressed, nor one without the sacraments shall act as a ‘Hotṛ’ at the Agnihotra.

11.s: narake hi patantyete juhvantaḥ sa ca yasya tat juhvataḥ tasmādvaitānakuśalo hotā syādvedapāragaḥ
11.d: नरके हि पतन्त्येते जुह्वन्तः स च यस्य तत् जुह्वतः तस्माद्वैतानकुशलो होता स्याद्वेदपारगः
11.e: If these persons pour the oblations, they sink into hell, as also the person to whom the agnihotra belongs; hence the ‘Hotṛ’ shall be a person fully learned in the Veda and expert in rituals.

11.s: prājāpatyamadattvā 'śvamagnyādheyasya dakṣiṇām anāhitāgnirbhavati brāhmaṇo vibhave sati
11.d: प्राजापत्यमदत्त्वा ऽश्वमग्न्याधेयस्य दक्षिणाम् अनाहिताग्निर्भवति ब्राह्मणो विभवे सति
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇa, possessed of wealth, does not give a ‘prājāpatya’ horse as the ‘fee’ foe the fire-laying, he becomes as good as one who has not laid the fire at all.

11.s: puṇyānyanyāni kurvīta śraddadhāno jitaindriyaḥ na tvalpadakṣiṇairyajñairyajetaiha kathaṃ cana
11.d: पुण्यान्यन्यानि कुर्वीत श्रद्दधानो जितैन्द्रियः न त्वल्पदक्षिणैर्यज्ञैर्यजेतैह कथं चन
11.e: The man who has faith and control over his senses may perform other meritorious acts; but he shall not, on any account, perform sacrifices with small fees.

11.s: indriyāṇi yaśaḥ svargamāyuḥ kīrtiṃ prajāḥ paśūn hantyalpadakṣiṇo yajñastasmānnālpadhano yajet
11.d: इन्द्रियाणि यशः स्वर्गमायुः कीर्तिं प्रजाः पशून् हन्त्यल्पदक्षिणो यज्ञस्तस्मान्नाल्पधनो यजेत्
11.e: A sacrifice with small fees destroys the organs, honour, heaven, longevity, fame, offspring and cattle. Hence one possessed of small means shall not perform sacrifices.

11.s: agnihotryapavidhyāgnīn brāhmaṇaḥ kāmakārataḥ cāndrāyaṇaṃ caren māsaṃ vīrahatyāsamaṃ hi tat
11.d: अग्निहोत्र्यपविध्याग्नीन् ब्राह्मणः कामकारतः चान्द्रायणं चरेन् मासं वीरहत्यासमं हि तत्
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇawho has set up the fires neglects them wilfully, he shall perform the ‘Cāndrāyaṇa’ penance for a month; as his offence is equal to the offence of killing a hero.

11.s: ye śūdrādadhigamyārthamagnihotramupāsate ṛtvijaste hi śūdrāṇāṃ brahmavādiṣu garhitāḥ
11.d: ये शूद्रादधिगम्यार्थमग्निहोत्रमुपासते ऋत्विजस्ते हि शूद्राणां ब्रह्मवादिषु गर्हिताः
11.e: Those who perform the Agnihotra, after having obtained wealth from aŚūdra, are ‘Śūdra’sPriests,’ censured among Vedic scholars.

11.s: teṣāṃ satatamajñānāṃ vṛṣalāgnyupasevinām padā mastakamākramya dātā durgāṇi saṃtaret
11.d: तेषां सततमज्ञानां वृषलाग्न्युपसेविनाम् पदा मस्तकमाक्रम्य दाता दुर्गाणि संतरेत्
11.e: The giver shall cut across his miseries by putting his foot upon the heads of those fools who attend upon theŚūdra’sfires.

11.s: akurvan vihitaṃ karma ninditaṃ ca samācaran prasaktaścaindriyārtheṣu prāyaścittīyate naraḥ prasajjanindriyārtheṣu
11.d: अकुर्वन् विहितं कर्म निन्दितं च समाचरन् प्रसक्तश्चैन्द्रियार्थेषु प्रायश्चित्तीयते नरः प्रसज्जनिन्द्रियार्थेषु
11.e: If a man does not do what is enjoined, or does what is censured, or becomes addicted to sensual objects, he becomes liable to expiatory rites.

11.s: akāmataḥ kṛte pāpe prāyaścittaṃ vidurbudhāḥ kāmakārakṛte 'pyāhureke śrutinidarśanāt
11.d: अकामतः कृते पापे प्रायश्चित्तं विदुर्बुधाः कामकारकृते ऽप्याहुरेके श्रुतिनिदर्शनात्
11.e: The learned understand Expiatory rites to pertain to cases where the sin is committed unintentionally; some people however assert on the evidence of ‘Śruti texts’ that they apply to cases of intentional offence also.

11.s: akāmataḥ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vedābhyāsena śudhyati kāmatastu kṛtaṃ mohāt prāyaścittaiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ
11.d: अकामतः कृतं पापं वेदाभ्यासेन शुध्यति कामतस्तु कृतं मोहात् प्रायश्चित्तैः पृथग्विधैः
11.e: A sin committed unintentionally is expiated by the reciting of the Veda; while that committed intentionally, in folly, is expiated by the various forms of expiatory rites.

11.s: prāyaścittīyatāṃ prāpya daivāt pūrvakṛtena vā na saṃsargaṃ vrajet sadbhiḥ prāyaścitte 'kṛte dvijaḥ
11.d: प्रायश्चित्तीयतां प्राप्य दैवात् पूर्वकृतेन वा न संसर्गं व्रजेत् सद्भिः प्रायश्चित्ते ऽकृते द्विजः
11.e: Having incurred the liability to an expiatory rite,—either by chance or by a previous deed,—a twice-born person shall not associate with righteous men, so long as the expiatory rite has not been performed.

11.s: iha duścaritaiḥ ke cit ke cit pūrvakṛtaistathā prāpnuvanti durātmāno narā rūpaviparyayam
11.d: इह दुश्चरितैः के चित् के चित् पूर्वकृतैस्तथा प्राप्नुवन्ति दुरात्मानो नरा रूपविपर्ययम्
11.e: Evil-minded men suffer disfigurement,—some from evil deeds committed during the present life and others from those committed in former lives.

11.s: suvarṇacauraḥ kaunakhyaṃ surāpaḥ śyāvadantatām brahmahā kṣayarogitvaṃ dauścarmyaṃ gurutalpagaḥ
11.d: सुवर्णचौरः कौनख्यं सुरापः श्यावदन्तताम् ब्रह्महा क्षयरोगित्वं दौश्चर्म्यं गुरुतल्पगः
11.e: The stealer of gold has disfigured nails; the drinker of wine, black teeth; the slayer of aBrāhmaṇa, consumption; and the violator of his preceptor’s bed, a disfigured skin;—(49) the informer, a foul-smelling nose; the false caluminator, a foul-smelling mouth; the stealer of grains, a deficiency of limbs; and the adulterator, an excess of limbs;—(50) the stealer of food, dyspepsia; the stealer of words, dumbness; the stealer of clothes, leucoderma; and the stealer of horse, lameness.—(51) It is thus that idiots, the dumb, the blind, the deaf and deformed men, despised by righteous men, are born, on account of particular acts.

11.s: piśunaḥ pautināsikyaṃ sūcakaḥ pūtivaktratām dhānyacauro 'ṅgahīnatvamātiraikyaṃ tu miśrakaḥ
11.d: पिशुनः पौतिनासिक्यं सूचकः पूतिवक्त्रताम् धान्यचौरो ऽङ्गहीनत्वमातिरैक्यं तु मिश्रकः
11.e: The stealer of gold has disfigured nails; the drinker of wine, black teeth; the slayer of aBrāhmaṇa, consumption; and the violator of his preceptor’s bed, a disfigured skin;—(49) the informer, a foul-smelling nose; the false caluminator, a foul-smelling mouth; the stealer of grains, a deficiency of limbs; and the adulterator, an excess of limbs;—(50) the stealer of food, dyspepsia; the stealer of words, dumbness; the stealer of clothes, leucoderma; and the stealer of horse, lameness.—(51) It is thus that idiots, the dumb, the blind, the deaf and deformed men, despised by righteous men, are born, on account of particular acts.

11.s: annahartā 'mayāvitvaṃ maukyaṃ vāgapahārakaḥ vastrāpahārakaḥ śvaitryaṃ paṅgutāmaśvahārakaḥ
11.d: अन्नहर्ता ऽमयावित्वं मौक्यं वागपहारकः वस्त्रापहारकः श्वैत्र्यं पङ्गुतामश्वहारकः
11.e: The stealer of gold has disfigured nails; the drinker of wine, black teeth; the slayer of aBrāhmaṇa, consumption; and the violator of his preceptor’s bed, a disfigured skin;—(49) the informer, a foul-smelling nose; the false caluminator, a foul-smelling mouth; the stealer of grains, a deficiency of limbs; and the adulterator, an excess of limbs;—(50) the stealer of food, dyspepsia; the stealer of words, dumbness; the stealer of clothes, leucoderma; and the stealer of horse, lameness.—(51) It is thus that idiots, the dumb, the blind, the deaf and deformed men, despised by righteous men, are born, on account of particular acts.

11.s: evaṃ karmaviśeṣeṇa jāyante sadvigarhitāḥ jaḍamūkāndhabadhirā vikṛtākṛtayastathā
11.d: एवं कर्मविशेषेण जायन्ते सद्विगर्हिताः जडमूकान्धबधिरा विकृताकृतयस्तथा
11.e: The stealer of gold has disfigured nails; the drinker of wine, black teeth; the slayer of aBrāhmaṇa, consumption; and the violator of his preceptor’s bed, a disfigured skin;—(49) the informer, a foul-smelling nose; the false caluminator, a foul-smelling mouth; the stealer of grains, a deficiency of limbs; and the adulterator, an excess of limbs;—(50) the stealer of food, dyspepsia; the stealer of words, dumbness; the stealer of clothes, leucoderma; and the stealer of horse, lameness.—(51) It is thus that idiots, the dumb, the blind, the deaf and deformed men, despised by righteous men, are born, on account of particular acts.

11.s: caritavyamato nityaṃ prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye nindyairhi lakṣaṇairyuktā jāyante 'niṣkṛtenasaḥ
11.d: चरितव्यमतो नित्यं प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्धये निन्द्यैर्हि लक्षणैर्युक्ता जायन्ते ऽनिष्कृतेनसः
11.e: Because persons with sins unexpiated are born with disgraceful marks, therefore expiatory rites shall always be performed, for the purpose of purification.

11.s: brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ mahānti pātakānyāhuḥ saṃsargaścāpi taiḥ saha
11.d: ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वङ्गनागमः महान्ति पातकान्याहुः संसर्गश्चापि तैः सह
11.e: Brāhmaṇa-slaying, wine-drinking, theft, intercourse with the Preceptor’s wife,—are called the ‘heinous offences,’ as also association with these.

11.s: anṛtaṃ ca samutkarṣe rājagāmi ca paiśunam guroścālīkanirbandhaḥ samāni brahmahatyayā
11.d: अनृतं च समुत्कर्षे राजगामि च पैशुनम् गुरोश्चालीकनिर्बन्धः समानि ब्रह्महत्यया
11.e: Lying for self-aggrandisement, caluminating before the king, and falsely harassing the Preceptor are equal to ‘Brāhmaṇa-killing.’

11.s: brahmaujjhatā vedanindā kauṭasākṣyaṃ suhṛdvadhaḥ garhitānādyayorjagdhiḥ surāpānasamāni ṣaṭ
11.d: ब्रह्मौज्झता वेदनिन्दा कौटसाक्ष्यं सुहृद्वधः गर्हितानाद्ययोर्जग्धिः सुरापानसमानि षट्
11.e: Neglecting the Veda, reviling the Veda, bearing false witness, slaying a friend, and eating of forbidden and unfit food,—these six are equal to ‘wine-drinking.’

11.s: nikṣepasyāpaharaṇaṃ narāśvarajatasya ca bhūmivajramaṇīnāṃ ca rukmasteyasamaṃ smṛtam
11.d: निक्षेपस्यापहरणं नराश्वरजतस्य च भूमिवज्रमणीनां च रुक्मस्तेयसमं स्मृतम्
11.e: Stealing of a deposit, or of men, horse, silver, land, diamonds and other oems,—all this has been declared to be equal to the ‘stealing of gold.’

11.s: retaḥsekaḥ svayonīṣu kumārīṣvantyajāsu ca sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣu gurutalpasamaṃ viduḥ
11.d: रेतःसेकः स्वयोनीषु कुमारीष्वन्त्यजासु च सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु गुरुतल्पसमं विदुः
11.e: Carnal intercourse with one’s uterine sister, or with virgins, or with low-born women, or with the women of one’s friend or son,—all this they regard as equal to the ‘violating of the Preceptor’s bed.’

11.s: govadho 'yājyasaṃyājyaṃ pāradāryātmavikrayaḥ gurumātṛpitṛtyāgaḥ svādhyāyāgnyoḥ sutasya ca
11.d: गोवधो ऽयाज्यसंयाज्यं पारदार्यात्मविक्रयः गुरुमातृपितृत्यागः स्वाध्यायाग्न्योः सुतस्य च
11.e: Killing a cow, sacrificing for one unworthy to sacrifice, adultery, selling oneself, abandoning one’s father, mother, teacher, or son, or of Vedic study or Fire;

11.s: parivittitā 'nuje 'nūḍhe parivedanameva ca tayordānaṃ ca kanyāyāstayoreva ca yājanam
11.d: परिवित्तिता ऽनुजे ऽनूढे परिवेदनमेव च तयोर्दानं च कन्यायास्तयोरेव च याजनम्
11.e: Allowing oneself to be superseded in marriage by his younger brother, superseding by the younger one’s elder brother in marriage, and the giving of one’s daughter to, or sacrificing for, these two;

11.s: kanyāyā dūṣaṇaṃ caiva vārdhuṣyaṃ vratalopanam taḍāgārāmadārāṇāmapatyasya ca vikrayaḥ
11.d: कन्याया दूषणं चैव वार्धुष्यं व्रतलोपनम् तडागारामदाराणामपत्यस्य च विक्रयः
11.e: Defiling a maiden, usury, breaking of a vow, selling a tank, a garden, one’s wife or a child.

11.s: vrātyatā bāndhavatyāgo bhṛtyādhyāpanameva ca bhṛtyā cādhyayanādānamapaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayaḥ bhṛtāccādhyayanādānam
11.d: व्रात्यता बान्धवत्यागो भृत्याध्यापनमेव च भृत्या चाध्ययनादानमपण्यानां च विक्रयः भृताच्चाध्ययनादानम्
11.e: Apostacy, abandoning a relative, teaching for wages, learning from a paid teacher and the selling of what should not be sold.

11.s: sarvākāreṣvadhīkāro mahāyantrapravartanam hiṃsauṣadhīnāṃ striājīvo 'bhicāro mūlakarma ca
11.d: सर्वाकारेष्वधीकारो महायन्त्रप्रवर्तनम् हिंसौषधीनां स्त्रिआजीवो ऽभिचारो मूलकर्म च
11.e: Superintending all mines, executing large mechanical works, destroying medicinal herbs, subsisting on women, performing malevolent rites and sorcery.

11.s: indhanārthamaśuṣkāṇāṃ drumāṇāmavapātanam ātmārthaṃ ca kriyārambho ninditānnādanaṃ tathā
11.d: इन्धनार्थमशुष्काणां द्रुमाणामवपातनम् आत्मार्थं च क्रियारम्भो निन्दितान्नादनं तथा
11.e: Cutting down green trees for purposes of fuel, the undertaking of the act (of cooking) for one’s own benefit and the eating of forbidden food.

11.s: anāhitāgnitā steyaṃ ṛṇānāmanapakriyā asatśāṣtrādhigamanaṃ kauśīlavyasya ca kriyā
11.d: अनाहिताग्निता स्तेयं ऋणानामनपक्रिया असत्शाष्त्राधिगमनं कौशीलव्यस्य च क्रिया
11.e: Omission of fire-laying, theft, non-payment of debts, studying bad books, and the practising of the histrionic art.

11.s: dhānyakupyapaśusteyaṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇam strīśūdraviśkṣatravadho nāstikyaṃ caupapātakam
11.d: धान्यकुप्यपशुस्तेयं मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणम् स्त्रीशूद्रविश्क्षत्रवधो नास्तिक्यं चौपपातकम्
11.e: Stealing grain, base metals and cattle,—intercourse with women addicted to drinking wine,—killing women,Śūdras,VaiśyasandKṣatriyas,—and heresy,—everyone of these is a ‘minor offence.’

11.s: brāhmaṇasya rujaḥ kṛtvā ghrātiraghreyamadyayoḥ rujaḥkṛtyaṃ jaihmyaṃ ca maithunaṃ puṃsi jātibhraṃśakaraṃ smṛtam
11.d: ब्राह्मणस्य रुजः कृत्वा घ्रातिरघ्रेयमद्ययोः रुजःकृत्यं जैह्म्यं च मैथुनं पुंसि जातिभ्रंशकरं स्मृतम्
11.e: Causing pain to aBrāhmaṇa,—smelling at things that should not be smelt, or at wine,—cheating—and sexual intercourse with a man,—all this is declared to lead to loss of caste.

11.s: kharāśvauṣṭramṛgaibhānāmajāvikavadhastathā saṅkarīkaraṇaṃ jñeyaṃ mīnāhimahiṣasya ca
11.d: खराश्वौष्ट्रमृगैभानामजाविकवधस्तथा सङ्करीकरणं ज्ञेयं मीनाहिमहिषस्य च
11.e: The killing of an ass, of a horse, of a camel, of a deer, of an elephant, of a goat, of a sheep, of fish, of a snake, and of a buffalo should be regarded as degrading the man to the rank of a ‘mixed caste.’

11.s: ninditebhyo dhanādānaṃ vāṇijyaṃ śūdrasevanam apātrīkaraṇaṃ jñeyamasatyasya ca bhāṣaṇam
11.d: निन्दितेभ्यो धनादानं वाणिज्यं शूद्रसेवनम् अपात्रीकरणं ज्ञेयमसत्यस्य च भाषणम्
11.e: Accepting gifts from despicable persons, trading, servingŚūdrasand the telling of a lie should be regarded as rendering one unworthy of receiving gifts.

11.s: kṛmikīṭavayohatyā madyānugatabhojanam phaledhaḥkusumasteyamadhairyaṃ ca malāvaham
11.d: कृमिकीटवयोहत्या मद्यानुगतभोजनम् फलेधःकुसुमस्तेयमधैर्यं च मलावहम्
11.e: The killing of insects, worms and birds,—the eating of things touched by wine,—the stealing of fruits, fuel or flowers—and inconstancy—are conducive to impurity.

11.s: etānyenāṃsi sarvāṇi yathauktāni pṛthak pṛthak yairyairvratairapohyante tāni samyalg nibodhata
11.d: एतान्येनांसि सर्वाणि यथौक्तानि पृथक् पृथक् यैर्यैर्व्रतैरपोह्यन्ते तानि सम्यल्ग् निबोधत
11.e: Learn properly now those penances b y which all these offences, severally described, become expiated.

11.s: brahmahā dvādaśa samāḥ kuṭīṃ kṛtvā vane vaset bhaikṣāśyātmaviśuddhyarthaṃ kṛtvā śavaśiro dhvajam
11.d: ब्रह्महा द्वादश समाः कुटीं कृत्वा वने वसेत् भैक्षाश्यात्मविशुद्ध्यर्थं कृत्वा शवशिरो ध्वजम्
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇa-slayer shall, for his purification, build a hut in the forest, live there for twelve years, subsisting on alms; making for himself a flag consisting of the head of the dead man.

11.s: lakṣyaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ vā syādviduṣāmicchayā 'tmanaḥ prāsyedātmānamagnau vā samiddhe triravākṣirāḥ
11.d: लक्ष्यं शस्त्रभृतां वा स्याद्विदुषामिच्छया ऽत्मनः प्रास्येदात्मानमग्नौ वा समिद्धे त्रिरवाक्षिराः
11.e: Or, by his own will, he should become the target of armed men cognisant (of his purpose); or he may thrice throw himself headlong into blazing fire.

11.s: yajeta vā 'śvamedhena svarjitā gosavena vā abhijidviśvajidbhyāṃ vā trivṛtā 'gniṣṭutā 'pi vā
11.d: यजेत वा ऽश्वमेधेन स्वर्जिता गोसवेन वा अभिजिद्विश्वजिद्भ्यां वा त्रिवृता ऽग्निष्टुता ऽपि वा
11.e: Or, he may offer theAśvamedha, or the Svajit—the Gosava, or the Abhijit—Viśvajit, or the tripleAgniṣṭut.

11.s: japan vā 'nyatamaṃ vedaṃ yojanānāṃ śataṃ vrajet brahmahatyāpanodāya mitabhujñiyataindriyaḥ
11.d: जपन् वा ऽन्यतमं वेदं योजनानां शतं व्रजेत् ब्रह्महत्यापनोदाय मितभुज्ञियतैन्द्रियः
11.e: Or, for the purpose of expiatingBrāhmaṇa-slay ing, he shall walk eight hundred miles, reciting one of the Vedas, eating little and controlling his senses.

11.s: sarvasvaṃ vedaviduṣe brāhmaṇāyaupapādayet dhanaṃ hi jīvanāyālaṃ gṛhaṃ vā saparicchadam
11.d: सर्वस्वं वेदविदुषे ब्राह्मणायौपपादयेत् धनं हि जीवनायालं गृहं वा सपरिच्छदम्
11.e: He shall make over to aBrāhmaṇalearned in the Veda, his entire property, which should be wealth sufficient for his maintenance,—or a house along with the furniture.

11.s: haviṣyabhug vā 'nusaret pratisrotaḥ sarasvatīm japedvā niyatāhārastrirvai vedasya saṃhitām
11.d: हविष्यभुग् वा ऽनुसरेत् प्रतिस्रोतः सरस्वतीम् जपेद्वा नियताहारस्त्रिर्वै वेदस्य संहिताम्
11.e: Or, subsisting on ‘sacrificial food,’ he may walk along each stream of theSarasvatī; or with food restrained, he may thrice recite the text of the Veda

11.s: kṛtavāpano nivasedgrāmānte govraje 'pi vā āśrame vṛkṣamūle vā gobrāhmaṇahite rataḥ
11.d: कृतवापनो निवसेद्ग्रामान्ते गोव्रजे ऽपि वा आश्रमे वृक्षमूले वा गोब्राह्मणहिते रतः
11.e: Having shaved off, he may dwell at the extremity of the village, or in a cow-pen, or in a hermitage under a tree,—giving himself up to doing good to cows andBrāhmaṇas.

11.s: brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā sadyaḥ prāṇān parityajet saṃyak prāṇān mucyate brahmahatyāyā goptā gorbrāhmaṇasya ca
11.d: ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा सद्यः प्राणान् परित्यजेत् संयक् प्राणान् मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्याया गोप्ता गोर्ब्राह्मणस्य च
11.e: He may give up his life unhesitatingly for the sake of a cow or aBrāhmaṇa; the protector of the cow and theBrāhmaṇabecomes absolved from the guilt ofBrāhmaṇa-killing.

11.s: trivāraṃ pratiroddhā vā sarvasvamavajitya vā tryavaraṃ viprasya tannimitte vā prāṇālābhe vimucyate prāṇālābhe 'pi mucyate
11.d: त्रिवारं प्रतिरोद्धा वा सर्वस्वमवजित्य वा त्र्यवरं विप्रस्य तन्निमित्ते वा प्राणालाभे विमुच्यते प्राणालाभे ऽपि मुच्यते
11.e: If he fights at least thrice on behalf of aBrāhmaṇa, or reconquers his entire property, or gives up his life for his sake,—he becomes absolved.

11.s: evaṃ dṛḍhavrato nityaṃ brahmacārī samāhitaḥ samāpte dvādaśe varṣe brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati
11.d: एवं दृढव्रतो नित्यं ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः समाप्ते द्वादशे वर्षे ब्रह्महत्यां व्यपोहति
11.e: He who remains thus firm in his vow, always chaste and with concentrated mind, shakes off the sin ofBrāhmaṇa-slaying, on the completion of the twelfth year.

11.s: śiṣṭvā vā bhūmidevānāṃ naradevasamāgame svameno 'vabhṛthasnāto hayamedhe vimucyate
11.d: शिष्ट्वा वा भूमिदेवानां नरदेवसमागमे स्वमेनो ऽवभृथस्नातो हयमेधे विमुच्यते
11.e: Or, having confessed his guilt before the congregation of the gods of Earth and the gods of men, if he bathes at the Final Bath of the Horse-sacrifice,—he becomes absolved.

11.s: dharmasya brāhmaṇo mūlamagraṃ rājanya ucyate tasmāt samāgame teṣāmeno vikhyāpya śudhyati
11.d: धर्मस्य ब्राह्मणो मूलमग्रं राजन्य उच्यते तस्मात् समागमे तेषामेनो विख्याप्य शुध्यति
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇais called the root of righteousness, and theKṣatriyaits top; hence one who confesses his guilt before their congregation becomes pure.

11.s: brahmaṇaḥ saṃbhavenaiva devānāmapi daivatam pramāṇaṃ caiva lokasya brahmātraiva hi kāraṇam
11.d: ब्रह्मणः संभवेनैव देवानामपि दैवतम् प्रमाणं चैव लोकस्य ब्रह्मात्रैव हि कारणम्
11.e: By his very birth theBrāhmaṇais a divinity even for the gods, and an authority for the people; and the Veda itself is the cause of this.

11.s: teṣāṃ vedavido brūyustrayo 'pyenaḥ suniṣkṛtim sā teṣāṃ pāvanāya syāt pavitrā viduṣāṃ hi vāk pavitraṃ
11.d: तेषां वेदविदो ब्रूयुस्त्रयो ऽप्येनः सुनिष्कृतिम् सा तेषां पावनाय स्यात् पवित्रा विदुषां हि वाक् पवित्रं
11.e: If even three of them, learned in the Veda, expound the expiation for the offences, that shall suffice for their purification; as the word of learned men is purificatory.

11.s: ato 'nyatamamāsthāya vidhiṃ vipraḥ samāhitaḥ brahmahatyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vyapohatyātmavattayā
11.d: अतो ऽन्यतममास्थाय विधिं विप्रः समाहितः ब्रह्महत्याकृतं पापं व्यपोहत्यात्मवत्तया
11.e: ABrāhmaṇawho, with concentrated mind, follows any one of these methods, removes, on account of his being self-possessed, the sin committed by killing aBrāhmaṇa.

11.s: hatvā garbhamavijñātametadeva vrataṃ caret rājanyavaiśyau caijānāvātreyīmeva ca striyam
11.d: हत्वा गर्भमविज्ञातमेतदेव व्रतं चरेत् राजन्यवैश्यौ चैजानावात्रेयीमेव च स्त्रियम्
11.e: Having killed an unknown embryo, one should perform this same penance,—also on killing aKṣatriyaor a Vaiśya, who has performed sacrifices, or a woman of the ‘Ātreyī’ race.

11.s: uktvā caivānṛtaṃ sākṣye pratirudhya guruṃ tathā pratirabhya apahṛtya ca niḥkṣepaṃ kṛtvā ca strīsuhṛtvadham nikṣepaṃ
11.d: उक्त्वा चैवानृतं साक्ष्ये प्रतिरुध्य गुरुं तथा प्रतिरभ्य अपहृत्य च निःक्षेपं कृत्वा च स्त्रीसुहृत्वधम् निक्षेपं
11.e: Similarly also for telling a lie in giving evidence, for angering the preceptor, for misappropriating a trust, and for killing one’s wife or friend.

11.s: iyaṃ viśuddhiruditā pramāpyākāmato dvijam kāmato brāhmaṇavadhe niṣkṛtirna vidhīyate
11.d: इयं विशुद्धिरुदिता प्रमाप्याकामतो द्विजम् कामतो ब्राह्मणवधे निष्कृतिर्न विधीयते
11.e: All this expiation has been laid down for killing aBrāhmaṇaunintentionally; for killing aBrāhmaṇaintentionally no atonement has been ordained.

11.s: surāṃ pītvā dvijo mohādagnivarṇāṃ surāṃ pibet tayā sa kāye nirdagdhe mucyate kilbiṣāt tataḥ
11.d: सुरां पीत्वा द्विजो मोहादग्निवर्णां सुरां पिबेत् तया स काये निर्दग्धे मुच्यते किल्बिषात् ततः
11.e: A twice-born person, having, through folly, drunk wine, shall drink wine red-hot; he becomes freed from his guilt, when his body has been completely burnt by it.

11.s: gomūtramagnivarṇaṃ vā pibedudakameva vā payo ghṛtaṃ vā 'maraṇādgośakṛdrasameva vā
11.d: गोमूत्रमग्निवर्णं वा पिबेदुदकमेव वा पयो घृतं वा ऽमरणाद्गोशकृद्रसमेव वा
11.e: Or, he may drink red-hot cow’s urine, or water, or milk, or butter, or liquid cow-dung, until he dies.

11.s: kaṇān vā bhakṣayedabdaṃ piṇyākaṃ vā sakṛtniśi surāpānāpanuttyarthaṃ vālavāsā jaṭī dhvajī
11.d: कणान् वा भक्षयेदब्दं पिण्याकं वा सकृत्निशि सुरापानापनुत्त्यर्थं वालवासा जटी ध्वजी
11.e: Or, for the expiation of the guilt of wine-drinking, he may, for one year, eat only once at night either pieces of grain or oil-cake, clothed in hair-cloth, with his hair matted, and carrying a sign.

11.s: surā vai malamannānāṃ pāpmā ca malamucyate tasmādbrāhmaṇarājanyau vaiśyaśca na surāṃ pibet
11.d: सुरा वै मलमन्नानां पाप्मा च मलमुच्यते तस्माद्ब्राह्मणराजन्यौ वैश्यश्च न सुरां पिबेत्
11.e: Wine indeed is the dirty refuse of grains, and sin also is called ‘dirt’; for this reason theBrāhmaṇa, theKṣatriyaand theVaiśyashall not drink wine.

11.s: gauḍī paiṣṭī ca mādhvī ca vijñeyā trividhā surā yathaivaikā tathā sarvā na pātavyā dvijottamaiḥ
11.d: गौडी पैष्टी च माध्वी च विज्ञेया त्रिविधा सुरा यथैवैका तथा सर्वा न पातव्या द्विजोत्तमैः
11.e: Wine should be understood to be of three kinds: (a) distilled from molasses (Gauḍī), (b) distilled from grains (Paiṣṭī), and (c) ‘distilled from grapes’ (Mādhvī); as the one so all the rest should never be drunk by the chief of the twice-born.

11.s: yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācānnaṃ madyaṃ māṃsaṃ surāsavam tadbrāhmaṇena nāttavyaṃ devānāmaśnatā haviḥ
11.d: यक्षरक्षःपिशाचान्नं मद्यं मांसं सुरासवम् तद्ब्राह्मणेन नात्तव्यं देवानामश्नता हविः
11.e: Intoxicants, meat, wine and distilled liquors are the food ofYakṣas,RākṣasasandPiśācas; it should not be taken by theBrāhmaṇawho partakes of the offerings to the gods.

11.s: amedhye vā paten matto vaidikaṃ vā 'pyudāharet akāryamanyat kuryādvā brāhmaṇo madamohitaḥ
11.d: अमेध्ये वा पतेन् मत्तो वैदिकं वा ऽप्युदाहरेत् अकार्यमन्यत् कुर्याद्वा ब्राह्मणो मदमोहितः
11.e: ABrāhmaṇa, stupefied by drunkenness, might tumble down upon unclean things; or he might wrongly recite the Veda; or he might do some other improper act.

11.s: yasya kāyagataṃ brahma madyenāplāvyate sakṛt tasya vyapaiti brāhmaṇyaṃ śūdratvaṃ ca sa gacchati
11.d: यस्य कायगतं ब्रह्म मद्येनाप्लाव्यते सकृत् तस्य व्यपैति ब्राह्मण्यं शूद्रत्वं च स गच्छति
11.e: When the ‘Brahman’ resident in his body has been once deluged by wine, the ‘Brāhmaṇahood’ disappears and the man becomes aŚūdra.

11.s: eṣā vicitrābhihitā surāpānasya niṣkṛtiḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi suvarṇasteyaniṣkṛtim
11.d: एषा विचित्राभिहिता सुरापानस्य निष्कृतिः अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि सुवर्णस्तेयनिष्कृतिम्
11.e: Thus have been described the various expiations for wine-drinking; after this I am going to expound the expiation for the theft of gold.

11.s: suvarṇasteyakṛdvipro rājānamabhigamya tu svakarma khyāpayan brūyātmāṃ bhavānanuśāstviti
11.d: सुवर्णस्तेयकृद्विप्रो राजानमभिगम्य तु स्वकर्म ख्यापयन् ब्रूयात्मां भवाननुशास्त्विति
11.e: ABrāhmaṇawho has committed the theft of gold shall go to the King, and confessing his crime, shall say ‘sire, punish me.’

11.s: gṛhītvā musalaṃ rājā sakṛddhanyāt tu taṃ svayam vadhena śudhyati steno brāhmaṇastapasaiva tu
11.d: गृहीत्वा मुसलं राजा सकृद्धन्यात् तु तं स्वयम् वधेन शुध्यति स्तेनो ब्राह्मणस्तपसैव तु
11.e: Taking up a club, the King himself shall strike him once. The thief becomes purified by death; but theBrāhmaṇaby penance alone.

11.s: tapasāpanunutsustu suvarṇasteyajaṃ malam cīravāsā dvijo 'raṇye caredbrahmahaṇo vratam
11.d: तपसापनुनुत्सुस्तु सुवर्णस्तेयजं मलम् चीरवासा द्विजो ऽरण्ये चरेद्ब्रह्महणो व्रतम्
11.e: If a twice-born person is desirous of removing the guilt of stealing gold by means of penance, he should perform the penance prescribed for the slayer of aBrāhmaṇa,—living in a forest, clothed in rags.

11.s: etairvratairapoheta pāpaṃ steyakṛtaṃ dvijaḥ gurustrīgamanīiyaṃ tu vratairebhirapānudet
11.d: एतैर्व्रतैरपोहेत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः गुरुस्त्रीगमनीइयं तु व्रतैरेभिरपानुदेत्
11.e: The twice-born man shall remove the guilt caused by theft by means of these penances. That caused by intercourse with the Preceptor’s wife he shall wipe off by means of these following penances.

11.s: gurutalpyabhibhāṣyainastapte svapyādayomaye talpe svapyād sūrmīṃ jvalantīṃ svāśliṣyen mṛtyunā sa viśudhyati vā 'śliṣyen
11.d: गुरुतल्प्यभिभाष्यैनस्तप्ते स्वप्यादयोमये तल्पे स्वप्याद् सूर्मीं ज्वलन्तीं स्वाश्लिष्येन् मृत्युना स विशुध्यति वा ऽश्लिष्येन्
11.e: He who has violated his Preceptor’s bed shall confess his crime and lie down upon a heated iron-bed; or embrace a blazing image. By death he becomes purified.

11.s: svayaṃ vā śiṣṇavṛṣaṇāvutkṛtyādhāya cāñjalau nairṛtīṃ diśamātiṣṭhedā nipātādajihmagaḥ
11.d: स्वयं वा शिष्णवृषणावुत्कृत्याधाय चाञ्जलौ नैरृतीं दिशमातिष्ठेदा निपातादजिह्मगः
11.e: Or, having cut off his penis and testicles, he shall take them in his joined hands and walk straight on towards the ‘region of evil spirits,’ until he falls down.

11.s: khaṭvāṅgī cīravāsā vā śmaśrulo vijane vane prājāpatyaṃ caret kṛcchramabdamekaṃ samāhitaḥ
11.d: खट्वाङ्गी चीरवासा वा श्मश्रुलो विजने वने प्राजापत्यं चरेत् कृच्छ्रमब्दमेकं समाहितः
11.e: Or, carrying a bedstead, clothed in rags, with beard grown, he shall perform, in the solitary forest, the ‘Prājāpatya’ penance, for one year, with concentrated mind.

11.s: cāndrāyaṇaṃ vā trīn māsānabhyasyenniyataindriyaḥ haviṣyeṇa yavāgvā vā gurutalpāpanuttaye
11.d: चान्द्रायणं वा त्रीन् मासानभ्यस्येन्नियतैन्द्रियः हविष्येण यवाग्वा वा गुरुतल्पापनुत्तये
11.e: Or, with his senses controlled, he shall perform the ‘Cāndrāyaṇa’ for three months, subsisting on ‘sacrificial food’ or on barley-gruel,—for the expiating of the sin of violating the Preceptor’s bed.

11.s: etairvratairapoheyurmahāpātakino malam upapātakinastvevamebhirnānāvidhairvrataiḥ
11.d: एतैर्व्रतैरपोहेयुर्महापातकिनो मलम् उपपातकिनस्त्वेवमेभिर्नानाविधैर्व्रतैः
11.e: By means of these penances, the committers of heinous crimes may wipe off their sins. The committers of minor offences may do the same by their following the several forms of penances.

11.s: upapātakasaṃyukto goghno māsaṃ yavān pibet kṛtavāpo vasedgoṣṭhe carmaṇā tena saṃvṛtaḥ
11.d: उपपातकसंयुक्तो गोघ्नो मासं यवान् पिबेत् कृतवापो वसेद्गोष्ठे चर्मणा तेन संवृतः
11.e: The cow-killer, charged with a minor offence, shall drink barley for three months; and having shaved his head and covered with the skin of the cow, he shall live in the cow-pen.

11.s: caturthakālamaśnīyādakṣāralavaṇaṃ mitam gomūtreṇācaret snānaṃ dvau māsau niyataindriyaḥ
11.d: चतुर्थकालमश्नीयादक्षारलवणं मितम् गोमूत्रेणाचरेत् स्नानं द्वौ मासौ नियतैन्द्रियः
11.e: For two months, with senses controlled, he shall eat a limited quantity of food, without any pungent salt, at the fourth meal-time; and shall bathe in cow’s urine.

11.s: divā 'nugacchedgāstāstu tiṣṭhannūrdhvaṃ rajaḥ pibet śuśrūṣitvā namaskṛtya rātrau vīrāsanaṃ vaset vīrāsano
11.d: दिवा ऽनुगच्छेद्गास्तास्तु तिष्ठन्नूर्ध्वं रजः पिबेत् शुश्रूषित्वा नमस्कृत्य रात्रौ वीरासनं वसेत् वीरासनो
11.e: During the day he shall follow those cows, and standing upright, inhale the dust; at night having attended and bowed to them, he shall rest in the ‘Vīrāsana’ posture.

11.s: tiṣṭhantīṣvanutiṣṭhet tu vrajantīṣvapyanuvrajet āsīnāsu tathā 'sīno niyato vītamatsaraḥ
11.d: तिष्ठन्तीष्वनुतिष्ठेत् तु व्रजन्तीष्वप्यनुव्रजेत् आसीनासु तथा ऽसीनो नियतो वीतमत्सरः
11.e: Self-controlled and free from greed, he shall stand when they stand, follow them when they move, and sit when they have sat down.

11.s: āturāmabhiśastāṃ vā cauravyāghrādibhirbhayaiḥ patitāṃ paṅkalagnaṃ vā sarvaupāyair vimocayet sarvaprāṇair
11.d: आतुरामभिशस्तां वा चौरव्याघ्रादिभिर्भयैः पतितां पङ्कलग्नं वा सर्वौपायैर् विमोचयेत् सर्वप्राणैर्
11.e: When a cow is sick, or threatened with danger from thieves, tigers and the like, or falls, or becomes stuck in a morass, he shall rescue her with all his strength.

11.s: uṣṇe varṣati śīte vā mārute vāti vā bhṛśam na kurvītātmanastrāṇaṃ gorakṛtvā tu śaktitaḥ
11.d: उष्णे वर्षति शीते वा मारुते वाति वा भृशम् न कुर्वीतात्मनस्त्राणं गोरकृत्वा तु शक्तितः
11.e: In heat, in rain, in cold, or when the wind is blowing violently, he shall not shelter himself, without having sheltered the cows to the best of his ability.

11.s: ātmano yadi vā 'nyeṣāṃ gṛhe kṣetre 'tha vā khale bhakṣayantīṃ na kathayet pibantaṃ caiva vatsakam
11.d: आत्मनो यदि वा ऽन्येषां गृहे क्षेत्रे ऽथ वा खले भक्षयन्तीं न कथयेत् पिबन्तं चैव वत्सकम्
11.e: If the cow is eating anything in his own or another’s house, field or threshing-yard,—or when her calf is drinking (her milk),—he shall not say anything.

11.s: anena vidhinā yastu goghno gāmanugacchati sa gohatyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tribhirmāsairvyapohati
11.d: अनेन विधिना यस्तु गोघ्नो गामनुगच्छति स गोहत्याकृतं पापं त्रिभिर्मासैर्व्यपोहति
11.e: The cow-killer, who attends upon cows in this manner, wipes off, in three months, the sin accruing from the killing of a cow—(115); and after having duly performed the penance, he shall give away cows with a bull as the eleventh; in the event of these being not available, he shall offer all he possesses to persons learned in the Veda.

11.s: vṛṣabhekādaśā gāśca dadyāt sucaritavrataḥ avidyamāne sarvasvaṃ vedavidbhyo nivedayet
11.d: वृषभेकादशा गाश्च दद्यात् सुचरितव्रतः अविद्यमाने सर्वस्वं वेदविद्भ्यो निवेदयेत्
11.e: The cow-killer, who attends upon cows in this manner, wipes off, in three months, the sin accruing from the killing of a cow—(115); and after having duly performed the penance, he shall give away cows with a bull as the eleventh; in the event of these being not available, he shall offer all he possesses to persons learned in the Veda.

11.s: etadeva vrataṃ kuryurupapātakino dvijāḥ avakīrṇivarjyaṃ śuddhyarthaṃ cāndrāyaṇamathāpi vā 'vakīrṇivarjaṃ
11.d: एतदेव व्रतं कुर्युरुपपातकिनो द्विजाः अवकीर्णिवर्ज्यं शुद्ध्यर्थं चान्द्रायणमथापि वा ऽवकीर्णिवर्जं
11.e: Twice-born men who have committed the minor offences, except the ‘immoral’ religious student, may, in order to purify themselves, perform this same penance, or the ‘Cāndrāyaṇa’ penance.

11.s: avakīrṇī tu kāṇena gardabhena catuṣpathe pākayajñavidhānena yajeta nirṛtiṃ niśi
11.d: अवकीर्णी तु काणेन गर्दभेन चतुष्पथे पाकयज्ञविधानेन यजेत निरृतिं निशि
11.e: The immoral religious student shall offer, at night, toNirṛti, on the crossway, a one-eyed ass, in the manner of the ‘Pākayajña.’

11.s: hutvā 'gnau vidhivaddhomānantataśca samaity ṛcā vātaindraguruvahnīnāṃ juhuyāt sarpiṣā 'hutīḥ
11.d: हुत्वा ऽग्नौ विधिवद्धोमानन्ततश्च समैत्य् ऋचा वातैन्द्रगुरुवह्नीनां जुहुयात् सर्पिषा ऽहुतीः
11.e: Having, in due form, poured oblations into the fire, he shall finally pour oblations of clarified butter toVāta,Indra, Guru and Vahni, with the verse ‘sam, etc.’

11.s: kāmato retasaḥ sekaṃ vratasthasya dvijanmanaḥ atikramaṃ vratasyāhurdharmajñā brahmavādinaḥ
11.d: कामतो रेतसः सेकं व्रतस्थस्य द्विजन्मनः अतिक्रमं व्रतस्याहुर्धर्मज्ञा ब्रह्मवादिनः
11.e: Persons learned in the Veda and knowing the law declare that for the twice-born person keeping up his vows, the intentional emission of semen means a ‘transgression of the vow.’

11.s: mārutaṃ puruhūtaṃ ca guruṃ pāvakameva ca caturo vratino 'bhyeti brāhmaṃ tejo 'vakīrṇinaḥ
11.d: मारुतं पुरुहूतं च गुरुं पावकमेव च चतुरो व्रतिनो ऽभ्येति ब्राह्मं तेजो ऽवकीर्णिनः
11.e: The spiritual power of the Religious Student, who has become ‘immoral,’ ‘goes away into the maruts, indra,Bṛhaspatiand agni.

11.s: etasminnenasi prāpte vasitvā gardabhājinam saptāgārāṃścaredbhaikṣaṃ svakarma parikīrtayan
11.d: एतस्मिन्नेनसि प्राप्ते वसित्वा गर्दभाजिनम् सप्तागारांश्चरेद्भैक्षं स्वकर्म परिकीर्तयन्
11.e: On this sin having been incurred, the man, clothed in the skin of the ass, shall go begging alms at seven houses; proclaiming his own deed.

11.s: tebhyo labdhena bhaikṣeṇa vartayannekakālikam upaspṛśaṃstriṣavaṇaṃ tvabdena sa viśudhyati triṣavaṇaṃ abdena
11.d: तेभ्यो लब्धेन भैक्षेण वर्तयन्नेककालिकम् उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं त्वब्देन स विशुध्यति त्रिषवणं अब्देन
11.e: Subsisting on a single meal per day out of the alms obtained from those houses, and bathing at the three ‘extractions,’ he becomes pure after one year.

11.s: jātibhraṃśakaraṃ karma kṛtvā 'nyatamamicchayā caret sāṃtapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ prājāpatyamanicchayā
11.d: जातिभ्रंशकरं कर्म कृत्वा ऽन्यतममिच्छया चरेत् सांतपनं कृच्छ्रं प्राजापत्यमनिच्छया
11.e: On having intention ally done any one of those acts which cause loss of caste, one should perform aSāntapana-Kṛcchra; and thePrājāpatya, when it is done unintentionally.

11.s: saṅkarāpātrakṛtyāsu māsaṃ śodhanamaindavam 'indavaḥ malinīkaraṇīyeṣu taptaḥ syādyāvakaistryaham
11.d: सङ्करापात्रकृत्यासु मासं शोधनमैन्दवम् ऽइन्दवः मलिनीकरणीयेषु तप्तः स्याद्यावकैस्त्र्यहम्
11.e: In the case of acts conducive to the degradation of ‘caste-mixture,’ or of those that make one unworthy of receiving gifts, purification is secured by the monthly lunar penance; and in the case of those that lead to defilement, one should mortify his body on barley-products for three days.

11.s: turīyo brahmahatyāyāḥ kṣatriyasya vadhe smṛtaḥ vaiśye 'ṣṭamāṃśo vṛttasthe śūdre jñeyastu ṣoḍaśaḥ
11.d: तुरीयो ब्रह्महत्यायाः क्षत्रियस्य वधे स्मृतः वैश्ये ऽष्टमांशो वृत्तस्थे शूद्रे ज्ञेयस्तु षोडशः
11.e: One fourth of the expiation for the killing of aBrāhmaṇahas been prescribed for the killing of aKṣatriya, one eighth for that of aVaiśya, and one sixteenth for that of aŚūdra,—each of these being one who is devoted to his duty.

11.s: akāmatastu rājanyaṃ vinipātya dvijottamaḥ vṛṣabhekasahasrā gā dadyāt sucaritavrataḥ
11.d: अकामतस्तु राजन्यं विनिपात्य द्विजोत्तमः वृषभेकसहस्रा गा दद्यात् सुचरितव्रतः
11.e: If the chief of twice-born men kills aKṣatriyaunintentionally, he should duly perform the penance and give away a thousand cows and a bull.

11.s: tryabdaṃ caredvā niyato jaṭī brahmahaṇo vratam vasan dūratare grāmādvṛkṣamūlaniketanaḥ
11.d: त्र्यब्दं चरेद्वा नियतो जटी ब्रह्महणो व्रतम् वसन् दूरतरे ग्रामाद्वृक्षमूलनिकेतनः
11.e: Or, he may perform, for three years, the penance of the ‘Brāhmaṇa-killer,’ keeping himself under control and wearing matted locks, living far off from the village, having his abode at the root of a tree.

11.s: etadeva caredabdaṃ prāyaścittaṃ dvijottamaḥ pramāpya vaiśyaṃ vṛttasthaṃ dadyāccaikaśataṃ dadyādvaikaśataṃ gavām
11.d: एतदेव चरेदब्दं प्रायश्चित्तं द्विजोत्तमः प्रमाप्य वैश्यं वृत्तस्थं दद्याच्चैकशतं दद्याद्वैकशतं गवाम्
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇakills a righteous Vaiśya, he shall perform this same expiatory rite for one year; or he may give a hundred cows and one (bull).

11.s: etadeva vrataṃ kṛtsnaṃ ṣaṇmāsāṃśūdrahā caret vṛṣabhekādaśā vā 'pi dadyādviprāya gāḥ sitāḥ
11.d: एतदेव व्रतं कृत्स्नं षण्मासांशूद्रहा चरेत् वृषभेकादशा वा ऽपि दद्याद्विप्राय गाः सिताः

11.s: mārjāranakulau hatvā cāṣaṃ maṇḍūkameva ca śvagodhaulūkakākāṃśca śūdrahatyāvrataṃ caret
11.d: मार्जारनकुलौ हत्वा चाषं मण्डूकमेव च श्वगोधौलूककाकांश्च शूद्रहत्याव्रतं चरेत्
11.e: Having killed a cat, an ichneumon, a blue jay, a frog, a dog, an iguana, an owl and a crow,—he shall perform the penance of the ‘Śūdra-killer.’

11.s: payaḥ pibet trirātraṃ vā yojanaṃ vā 'dhvano vrajet upaspṛśet sravantyāṃ vā sūktaṃ vā 'bdaivataṃ japet
11.d: पयः पिबेत् त्रिरात्रं वा योजनं वा ऽध्वनो व्रजेत् उपस्पृशेत् स्रवन्त्यां वा सूक्तं वा ऽब्दैवतं जपेत्
11.e: Or, he may drink milk only for three days, or walk over eight hundred miles of road, or bathe in a stream, or recite the hymn addressed to the Waters.

11.s: abhriṃ kārṣṇāyasīṃ dadyāt sarpaṃ hatvā dvijottamaḥ palālabhārakaṃ ṣaṇḍhe saisakaṃ caikamāṣakam
11.d: अभ्रिं कार्ष्णायसीं दद्यात् सर्पं हत्वा द्विजोत्तमः पलालभारकं षण्ढे सैसकं चैकमाषकम्
11.e: For killing a snake, theBrāhmaṇashould give an iron spade; and in the case of a eunuch, a load of straw and a ‘māsa’ of lead.

11.s: ghṛtakumbhaṃ varāhe tu tiladroṇaṃ tu tittirau śuke dvihāyanaṃ vatsaṃ krauñcaṃ hatvā trihāyanam
11.d: घृतकुम्भं वराहे तु तिलद्रोणं तु तित्तिरौ शुके द्विहायनं वत्सं क्रौञ्चं हत्वा त्रिहायनम्
11.e: For a boar, a jar of clarified butter; for a partridge, a ‘droṇa’ of sesamum; for a parrot, a two-year-old calf; and for killing a horse, a three-year-old calf.

11.s: hatvā haṃsaṃ balākāṃ ca bakaṃ barhiṇameva ca vānaraṃ śyenabhāsau ca sparśayedbrāhmaṇāya gām
11.d: हत्वा हंसं बलाकां च बकं बर्हिणमेव च वानरं श्येनभासौ च स्पर्शयेद्ब्राह्मणाय गाम्
11.e: On having killed a swan, abalākā, a crane, a peacock, a monkey, a falcon, or a vulture,—one should give a cow to aBrāhmaṇa.

11.s: vāso dadyāddhayaṃ hatvā pañca nīlān vṛṣān gajam ajameṣāvanaḍvāhaṃ kharaṃ hatvaikahāyanam
11.d: वासो दद्याद्धयं हत्वा पञ्च नीलान् वृषान् गजम् अजमेषावनड्वाहं खरं हत्वैकहायनम्
11.e: On killing a horse, one should give a garment; and five black bulls on killing an elephant; on killing a goat and a sheep, an ox; and on killing a hare, a one-year-old calf.

11.s: kravyādāṃstu mṛgān hatvā dhenuṃ dadyāt payasvinīm akravyādān vatsatarīmuṣṭraṃ hatvā tu kṛṣṇalam
11.d: क्रव्यादांस्तु मृगान् हत्वा धेनुं दद्यात् पयस्विनीम् अक्रव्यादान् वत्सतरीमुष्ट्रं हत्वा तु कृष्णलम्
11.e: For killing carnivorous animals, one should give a milch-cow; and a heifer for killing those not carnivorous; and a ‘kṛṣṇala’ of gold for killing a camel.

11.s: jīnakārmukabastāvīn pṛthag dadyādviśuddhaye caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ nārīrhatvā 'navasthitāḥ
11.d: जीनकार्मुकबस्तावीन् पृथग् दद्याद्विशुद्धये चतुर्णामपि वर्णानां नारीर्हत्वा ऽनवस्थिताः
11.e: For killing inconstant women of the four castes, one should give, for his purification, a leathern bag, a bow, a goat and a sheep respectively.

11.s: dānena vadhanirṇekaṃ sarpādīnāmaśaknuvan ekaikaśaścaret kṛcchraṃ dvijaḥ pāpāpanuttaye
11.d: दानेन वधनिर्णेकं सर्पादीनामशक्नुवन् एकैकशश्चरेत् कृच्छ्रं द्विजः पापापनुत्तये
11.e: If a twice-born person is unable to atone the sin of killing by means of gifts, he should perform the ‘Kṛcchra,’ for each act, for the purpose of removing his sin.

11.s: asthimatāṃ tu sattvānāṃ sahasrasya pramāpaṇe pūrṇe cānasyanasthnāṃ tu śūdrahatyāvrataṃ caret
11.d: अस्थिमतां तु सत्त्वानां सहस्रस्य प्रमापणे पूर्णे चानस्यनस्थ्नां तु शूद्रहत्याव्रतं चरेत्
11.e: If one kills one thousand animals ‘with bones,’ or a full cart-load of boneless ones, he shall perform the penance for the killing of aŚūdra.

11.s: kiṃ cideva tu viprāya dadyādasthimatāṃ vadhe anasthnāṃ caiva hiṃsāyāṃ prāṇāyāmena śudhyati
11.d: किं चिदेव तु विप्राय दद्यादस्थिमतां वधे अनस्थ्नां चैव हिंसायां प्राणायामेन शुध्यति
11.e: For the killing of animals with bones, he should give some trifle to aBrāhmaṇa; and for the killing of boneless animals, one becomes purified by the ‘control of breath.’

11.s: phaladānāṃ tu vṛkṣāṇāṃ chedane japyaṃ ṛcśatam gulmavallīlatānāṃ ca puṣpitānāṃ ca vīrudhām
11.d: फलदानां तु वृक्षाणां छेदने जप्यं ऋच्शतम् गुल्मवल्लीलतानां च पुष्पितानां च वीरुधाम्
11.e: When one cuts fruit-bearing trees, shrubs, creepers, branches of trees or flowering plants, he should recite one hundredṚkverses.

11.s: annādyajānāṃ sattvānāṃ rasajānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ phalapuṣpaudbhavānāṃ ca ghṛtaprāśo viśodhanam
11.d: अन्नाद्यजानां सत्त्वानां रसजानां च सर्वशः फलपुष्पौद्भवानां च घृतप्राशो विशोधनम्
11.e: For the destroying of any kind of creatures bred in food, in sauces, in fruits or in flowers, the expiation consists in eating with clarified butter.

11.s: kṛṣtajānāmoṣadhīnāṃ jātānāṃ ca svayaṃ vane vṛthālambhe 'nugacchedgāṃ dinamekaṃ payovrataḥ
11.d: कृष्तजानामोषधीनां जातानां च स्वयं वने वृथालम्भे ऽनुगच्छेद्गां दिनमेकं पयोव्रतः
11.e: If one needlessly cuts plants grown by cultivation, or those that spontaneously grow in the forest, he shall attend on the cow for one day, subsisting on milk only.

11.s: etairvratairapohyaṃ syādeno hiṃsāsamudbhavam jñānājñānakṛtaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śṛṇutānādyabhakṣaṇe
11.d: एतैर्व्रतैरपोह्यं स्यादेनो हिंसासमुद्भवम् ज्ञानाज्ञानकृतं कृत्स्नं शृणुतानाद्यभक्षणे
11.e: By means of these penances shall one remove the six arising from the act of slaying, either intentionally or unintentionally. Now listen to all that is involved in eating forbidden food.

11.s: ajñānādvāruṇīṃ pītvā saṃskāreṇaiva śudhyati matipūrvamanirdeśyaṃ prāṇāntikamiti sthitiḥ
11.d: अज्ञानाद्वारुणीं पीत्वा संस्कारेणैव शुध्यति मतिपूर्वमनिर्देश्यं प्राणान्तिकमिति स्थितिः
11.e: If one drinks wine unintentionally, he becomes pure by a sacrament; this, however, is not what should be prescribed in the case of doing the act intentionally; in which case there should be a penance involving death;—such is the settled law.

11.s: apaḥ surābhājanasthā madyabhāṇḍasthitāstathā pañcarātraṃ pibet pītvā śaṅkhapuṣpīśṛtaṃ payaḥ
11.d: अपः सुराभाजनस्था मद्यभाण्डस्थितास्तथा पञ्चरात्रं पिबेत् पीत्वा शङ्खपुष्पीशृतं पयः
11.e: If one has drunk water kept in a vessel used for keeping wine, or in a pot where intoxicating drinks are kept, he shall drink, for five days, milk in whichŚaṅkhapuṣpīhas been boiled.

11.s: spṛṣṭva dattvā ca madirāṃ vidhivat pratigṛhya ca śūdraucchiṣṭāśca pītvā 'paḥ kuśavāri pibet tryaham
11.d: स्पृष्ट्व दत्त्वा च मदिरां विधिवत् प्रतिगृह्य च शूद्रौच्छिष्टाश्च पीत्वा ऽपः कुशवारि पिबेत् त्र्यहम्
11.e: If one touches wine, or offers it to another, or receives it in due form,—or if he drinks water left by aŚūdra,—he shall drink kuśa-water for three days.

11.s: brāhmaṇastu surāpasya gandhamāghrāya somapaḥ prāṇānapsu trirāyamya ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati
11.d: ब्राह्मणस्तु सुरापस्य गन्धमाघ्राय सोमपः प्राणानप्सु त्रिरायम्य घृतं प्राश्य विशुध्यति
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇawho has partaken of the Soma inhales the odour given out by a wine-drinker, he becomes pure by thrice suppressing his breath in water and eating clarified butter.

11.s: ajñānāt prāśya viṣmūtraṃ surāsaṃspṛṣṭameva ca punaḥ saṃskāramarhanti trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ
11.d: अज्ञानात् प्राश्य विष्मूत्रं सुरासंस्पृष्टमेव च पुनः संस्कारमर्हन्ति त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः
11.e: The three twice-born castes, who have unwittingly swallowed ordure or urine, or anything that has been in contact with wine, are liable to re-initiation.

11.s: vapanaṃ mekhalā daṇḍo bhaikṣacaryā vratāni ca bhaikṣyacaryā nivartante dvijātīnāṃ punaḥsaṃskārakarmaṇi
11.d: वपनं मेखला दण्डो भैक्षचर्या व्रतानि च भैक्ष्यचर्या निवर्तन्ते द्विजातीनां पुनःसंस्कारकर्मणि
11.e: In the performance of the Re-initiation of twice-born men, tonsure, the girdle, the staff, begging alms, and the vows are omitted.

11.s: abhojyānāṃ tu bhuktvā 'nnaṃ strīśūdraucchiṣṭameva ca jagdhvā māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ ca saptarātraṃ yavān pibet
11.d: अभोज्यानां तु भुक्त्वा ऽन्नं स्त्रीशूद्रौच्छिष्टमेव च जग्ध्वा मांसमभक्ष्यं च सप्तरात्रं यवान् पिबेत्
11.e: If one has eaten the food of persons of unfit food, or food left by a woman or aŚūdra,—or forbidden flesh,—he shall drink barley for seven days.

11.s: śuktāni ca kaṣāyāṃśca pītvā medhyānyapi dvijaḥ tāvadbhavatyaprayato yāvat tanna vrajatyadhaḥ
11.d: शुक्तानि च कषायांश्च पीत्वा मेध्यान्यपि द्विजः तावद्भवत्यप्रयतो यावत् तन्न व्रजत्यधः
11.e: If a twice-born person drinks soured liquids or decoctions,—even though they be pure,—remains impure until it has gone down.

11.s: viḍvarāhakharauṣtrāṇāṃ gomāyoḥ kapikākayoḥ prāśya mūtrapurīṣāṇi dvijaścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret
11.d: विड्वराहखरौष्त्राणां गोमायोः कपिकाकयोः प्राश्य मूत्रपुरीषाणि द्विजश्चान्द्रायणं चरेत्
11.e: If a twice-born person swallows the ordure or urine of the village-pig, of an ass, of a camel, of a jackal, of a monkey, or of a crow—he shall perform theCāndrāyaṇa.

11.s: śuṣkāṇi bhuktvā māṃsāni bhaumāni kavakāni ca ajñātaṃ caiva sūnāsthametadeva vrataṃ caret
11.d: शुष्काणि भुक्त्वा मांसानि भौमानि कवकानि च अज्ञातं चैव सूनास्थमेतदेव व्रतं चरेत्
11.e: If one eats dried meat, mushrooms growing on the ground, or unrecognised meat lying in the slaughter-house—he shall perform this same penance.

11.s: kravyādasūkarauṣṭrāṇāṃ kukkuṭānāṃ ca bhakṣaṇe narakākakharāṇāṃ ca taptakṛcchraṃ viśodhanam
11.d: क्रव्यादसूकरौष्ट्राणां कुक्कुटानां च भक्षणे नरकाकखराणां च तप्तकृच्छ्रं विशोधनम्
11.e: For eating the meat of carnivorous animals, of pigs, of camels, of cocks, of crows, of asses, or of human flesh,—the atonement consists of theTapta-Kṛcchra.

11.s: māsikānnaṃ tu yo 'śnīyādasamāvartako dvijaḥ sa trīṇyahānyupavasedekāhaṃ caudake vaset
11.d: मासिकान्नं तु यो ऽश्नीयादसमावर्तको द्विजः स त्रीण्यहान्युपवसेदेकाहं चौदके वसेत्
11.e: If a twice-born person, who has not completed his course of study, eats food given at a monthly rite, he shall fast for three days and remain one day in water.

11.s: brahmacārī tu yo 'śnīyān madhu māṃsaṃ kathaṃ cana vratacārī tu sa kṛtvā prākṛtaṃ kṛcchraṃ vrataśeṣaṃ samāpayet
11.d: ब्रह्मचारी तु यो ऽश्नीयान् मधु मांसं कथं चन व्रतचारी तु स कृत्वा प्राकृतं कृच्छ्रं व्रतशेषं समापयेत्
11.e: If a person keeping a vow happens, in any way, to eat honey or meat, he should perform the originalKṛcchra, and then complete the remainder of his vow.

11.s: biḍālakākākhūcchiṣṭaṃ jagdhvā śvanakulasya ca keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca pibedbrahmasuvarcalām
11.d: बिडालकाकाखूच्छिष्टं जग्ध्वा श्वनकुलस्य च केशकीटावपन्नं च पिबेद्ब्रह्मसुवर्चलाम्
11.e: He who eats what has been left by a cat, a crow, a rat, a dog, or an ichneumon,—or food defiled by a hair or an insect,—shall drink theBrahmasuvarcalāherb.

11.s: abhojyamannaṃ nāttavyamātmanaḥ śuddhimicchatā ajñānabhuktaṃ tūttāryaṃ śodhyaṃ vā 'pyāśu śodhanaiḥ
11.d: अभोज्यमन्नं नात्तव्यमात्मनः शुद्धिमिच्छता अज्ञानभुक्तं तूत्तार्यं शोध्यं वा ऽप्याशु शोधनैः
11.e: If one desires his own purity, he should not eat improper food; when eaten unintentionally, it should be thrown out, or speedily atoned for by means of purifications.

11.s: eṣo 'nādyādanasyaukto vratānāṃ vividho vidhiḥ steyadoṣāpahartr̥̄ṇāṃ vratānāṃ śrūyatāṃ vidhiḥ
11.d: एषो ऽनाद्यादनस्यौक्तो व्रतानां विविधो विधिः स्तेयदोषापहर्त्र्̥̄णां व्रतानां श्रूयतां विधिः
11.e: Thus has the law relating to the penances for the eating of improper food been set forth; listen now to the law relating to the penances expiatory of the sins of theft.

11.s: dhānyānnadhanacauryāṇi kṛtvā kāmāddvijottamaḥ svajātīyagṛhādeva kṛcchrābdena viśudhyati
11.d: धान्यान्नधनचौर्याणि कृत्वा कामाद्द्विजोत्तमः स्वजातीयगृहादेव कृच्छ्राब्देन विशुध्यति
11.e: If a chief of twice-born men intentionally commits theft of grains, cooked food and wealth, from the house of a caste-fellow, he becomes pure by performing theKṛcchrafor one year.

11.s: manuṣyāṇāṃ tu haraṇe strīṇāṃ kṣetragṛhasya ca kūpavāpījalānāṃ ca śuddhiścāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam
11.d: मनुष्याणां तु हरणे स्त्रीणां क्षेत्रगृहस्य च कूपवापीजलानां च शुद्धिश्चान्द्रायणं स्मृतम्
11.e: For the stealing of men and women, of a field or a house, or the water of a well, or a tank,—theCāndrāyaṇahas been declared to be the expiation.

11.s: dravyāṇāmalpasārāṇāṃ steyaṃ kṛtvā 'nyaveśmataḥ kṛtvā 'nyaveśmani caret sāṃtapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ tanniryātyātmaśuddhaye
11.d: द्रव्याणामल्पसाराणां स्तेयं कृत्वा ऽन्यवेश्मतः कृत्वा ऽन्यवेश्मनि चरेत् सांतपनं कृच्छ्रं तन्निर्यात्यात्मशुद्धये
11.e: If one steals things of small value in the house of another, he should restore them; and for his own purification, he should perform the ‘Sāntapana Kṛcchra.’

11.s: bhakṣyabhojyāpaharaṇe yānaśayyā ''sanasya ca puṣpamūlaphalānāṃ ca pañcagavyaṃ viśodhanam
11.d: भक्ष्यभोज्यापहरणे यानशय्या 'ऽसनस्य च पुष्पमूलफलानां च पञ्चगव्यं विशोधनम्
11.e: For the stealing of eatables and edibles, of a conveyance or a bed, or a seat, or of fruits, roots and flowers,—the expiation consists of the Five Products of the cow.

11.s: tṛṇakāṣṭhadrumāṇāṃ ca śuṣkānnasya guḍasya ca celacarmāmiṣāṇāṃ ca trirātraṃ syādabhojanam cailacarmāmikṣāṇāṃ
11.d: तृणकाष्ठद्रुमाणां च शुष्कान्नस्य गुडस्य च चेलचर्मामिषाणां च त्रिरात्रं स्यादभोजनम् चैलचर्मामिक्षाणां
11.e: There should be fasting for three days, in the case of stealing grass, wood, trees, dry food, molasses, clothes, leather and meat.

11.s: maṇimuktāpravālānāṃ tāmrasya rajatasya ca ayaḥkāṃsyaupalānāṃ ca dvādaśāhaṃ kaṇānnatā
11.d: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानां ताम्रस्य रजतस्य च अयःकांस्यौपलानां च द्वादशाहं कणान्नता
11.e: In the case of the stealing of gems, pearls, corals, copper, silver, iron, bronze and stone, one should subsist, for twelve days, on pieces of grain.

11.s: kārpāsakīṭajaurṇānāṃ dviśaphekaśaphasya ca dveśaphekakhurasya ca pakṣigandhoṣadhīnāṃ ca rajjvāścaiva tryahaṃ payaḥ
11.d: कार्पासकीटजौर्णानां द्विशफेकशफस्य च द्वेशफेकखुरस्य च पक्षिगन्धोषधीनां च रज्ज्वाश्चैव त्र्यहं पयः
11.e: In the case of cotton, silk, wool, an animal with cleft hoofs, an animal with uncleft hoofs, a bird, perfumes, medicinal herbs, and a rope,—milk shall be drunk for three days.

11.s: etairvratairapoheta pāpaṃ steyakṛtaṃ dvijaḥ agamyāgamanīyaṃ tu vratairebhirapānudet
11.d: एतैर्व्रतैरपोहेत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः अगम्यागमनीयं तु व्रतैरेभिरपानुदेत्
11.e: By means of these penances, the twice-born man shall remove the sin caused by theft; that due to approaching women who should not be approached, he shall expiate by these (following) penances.

11.s: gurutalpavrataṃ kuryādretaḥ siktvā svayoniṣu sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣu kumārīṣvantyajāsu ca
11.d: गुरुतल्पव्रतं कुर्याद्रेतः सिक्त्वा स्वयोनिषु सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु कुमारीष्वन्त्यजासु च
11.e: If one has had sexual intercourse with his uterine sister, or with the wife of his friend, or of his son, or with an unmarried maiden, or with a lowest-born woman,—he should perform the penance prescribed for the ‘violation of the Preceptor’s Bed.’

11.s: paitṛsvaseyīṃ bhaginīṃ svasrīyāṃ mātureva ca mātuśca bhrātustanayāṃ gatvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret [bhrāturāptasya gatvā
11.d: पैतृस्वसेयीं भगिनीं स्वस्रीयां मातुरेव च मातुश्च भ्रातुस्तनयां गत्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् [भ्रातुराप्तस्य गत्वा
11.e: On having had intercourse with one’s sister born of his father’s sister, or of his mother’s sister, or of his mother’s full brother,—one should perform theCāndrāyaṇa.

11.s: etāstisrastu bhāryārthe naupayacchet tu buddhimān jñātitvenānupeyāstāḥ patati hyupayannadhaḥ
11.d: एतास्तिस्रस्तु भार्यार्थे नौपयच्छेत् तु बुद्धिमान् ज्ञातित्वेनानुपेयास्ताः पतति ह्युपयन्नधः
11.e: A wise man should never take these three as his wife; being blood-relations, they are not fit to be married; because by marrying them one sinks low.

11.s: amānuṣīṣū puruṣa udakyāyāmayoniṣu retaḥ siktvā jale caiva kṛcchraṃ sāṃtapanaṃ caret
11.d: अमानुषीषू पुरुष उदक्यायामयोनिषु रेतः सिक्त्वा जले चैव कृच्छ्रं सांतपनं चरेत्
11.e: A man who has had sexual intercourse with nonhuman females, or with a menstruating woman,—and he who has discharged his semen in a place other than the female organ, or in water,—should perporm the ‘Sāntapana Kṛcchra.’

11.s: maithunaṃ tu samāsevya puṃsi yoṣiti vā dvijaḥ goyāne 'psu divā caiva savāsāḥ snānamācaret
11.d: मैथुनं तु समासेव्य पुंसि योषिति वा द्विजः गोयाने ऽप्सु दिवा चैव सवासाः स्नानमाचरेत्
11.e: If a twice-born man commits an unnatural offence with a male, or has intercourse with a female, in an ox-cart, or in water, or during the day,—he should take a bath along with his clothes.

11.s: caṇḍālāntyastriyo gatvā bhuktvā ca pratigṛhya ca patatyajñānato vipro jñānāt sāmyaṃ tu gacchati
11.d: चण्डालान्त्यस्त्रियो गत्वा भुक्त्वा च प्रतिगृह्य च पतत्यज्ञानतो विप्रो ज्ञानात् साम्यं तु गच्छति
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇaunintentionally approaches a woman of theCaṇḍālaor other lowest-born castes,—or eats her food, or receives her presents,—he becomes an outcast; but if he does it intentionally, he becomes her equal.

11.s: vipraduṣṭāṃ striyaṃ bhartā nirundhyādekaveśmani yat puṃsaḥ paradāreṣu taccaināṃ cārayedvratam
11.d: विप्रदुष्टां स्त्रियं भर्ता निरुन्ध्यादेकवेश्मनि यत् पुंसः परदारेषु तच्चैनां चारयेद्व्रतम्
11.e: If the wife is particularly corrupt, her husband should keep her confined in one room, and should make her perform that penance which has been prescribed for males in cases of adultery.

11.s: sā cet punaḥ praduṣyet tu sadṛśenaupamantritā sadṛśenaupayantritā ? kṛcchraṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ caiva tadasyāḥ pāvanaṃ smṛtam
11.d: सा चेत् पुनः प्रदुष्येत् तु सदृशेनौपमन्त्रिता सदृशेनौपयन्त्रिता ? कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं चैव तदस्याः पावनं स्मृतम्
11.e: If she happens to be corrupted again, on being solicited by a man of equal caste,—then theKṛcchraand theCāndrāyaṇawould be the means prescribed for her purification.

11.s: yat karotyekarātreṇa vṛṣalīsevanāddvijaḥ tadbhaikṣabhujjapannityaṃ tribhirvarṣairvyapohati
11.d: यत् करोत्येकरात्रेण वृषलीसेवनाद्द्विजः तद्भैक्षभुज्जपन्नित्यं त्रिभिर्वर्षैर्व्यपोहति
11.e: What a twice-born man commits by dallying with aCaṇḍālīfor one night,—that he wipes off in three years, living on alms and constantly repeating (sacred texts).

11.s: eṣā pāpakṛtāmuktā caturṇāmapi niṣkṛtiḥ patitaiḥ saṃprayuktānāmimāḥ śṛṇuta niṣkṛtīḥ
11.d: एषा पापकृतामुक्ता चतुर्णामपि निष्कृतिः पतितैः संप्रयुक्तानामिमाः शृणुत निष्कृतीः
11.e: Thus has the atonement tor the four kinds of sinners been set forth; now listen to these (following) expiations for those who associate with outcasts.

11.s: saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena sahācaran yājanādhyāpanādyaunātna tu yānāsanāśanāt
11.d: संवत्सरेण पतति पतितेन सहाचरन् याजनाध्यापनाद्यौनात्न तु यानासनाशनात्
11.e: If one associates with an outcast for one year, he himself becomes an outcast; not by sacrificing for him, or teaching him, or forming a matrimonial alliance with him,—but by walking, sitting or eating.

11.s: yo yena patitenaiṣāṃ saṃsargaṃ yāti mānavaḥ sa tasyaiva vrataṃ kuryāt tatsaṃsargaviśuddhaye
11.d: यो येन पतितेनैषां संसर्गं याति मानवः स तस्यैव व्रतं कुर्यात् तत्संसर्गविशुद्धये
11.e: When a man associates with any one of outcasts, he should, for his own purification, perform the same penance that has been prescribed for that outcast.

11.s: patitasyaudakaṃ kāryaṃ sapiṇḍairbāndhavairbahiḥ nindite 'hani sāyāhne jñātiṛtvijgurusaṃnidhau
11.d: पतितस्यौदकं कार्यं सपिण्डैर्बान्धवैर्बहिः निन्दिते ऽहनि सायाह्ने ज्ञातिऋत्विज्गुरुसंनिधौ
11.e: When one has become an outcast, hisSapiṇḍasand relations shall offer him ‘water’ outside, on an inauspicious day, in the evening, in the presence of relatives, priests and elders.

11.s: dāsī ghaṭamapāṃ pūrṇaṃ paryasyet pretavat padā ahorātramupāsīrannaśaucaṃ bāndhavaiḥ saha
11.d: दासी घटमपां पूर्णं पर्यस्येत् प्रेतवत् पदा अहोरात्रमुपासीरन्नशौचं बान्धवैः सह
11.e: A female slave shall overturn a jar full of water with her foot, as in the case of the dead; and they, along with the relations, shall observe the ‘uncleanliness’ for the day and night.

11.s: nivarteraṃśca tasmāt tu saṃbhāṣaṇasahāsane dāyādyasya pradānaṃ ca yātrā caiva hi laukikī
11.d: निवर्तेरंश्च तस्मात् तु संभाषणसहासने दायाद्यस्य प्रदानं च यात्रा चैव हि लौकिकी
11.e: Thenceforth shall cease all conversation with him, sitting with him, his sharing in property, as also all ordinary intercourse.

11.s: jyeṣṭhatā ca nivarteta jyeṣṭhāvāpyaṃ ca yaddhanam yadvasu jyeṣṭhāṃśaṃ prāpnuyāccāsya yavīyān guṇato 'dhikaḥ
11.d: ज्येष्ठता च निवर्तेत ज्येष्ठावाप्यं च यद्धनम् यद्वसु ज्येष्ठांशं प्राप्नुयाच्चास्य यवीयान् गुणतो ऽधिकः
11.e: The right of primogeniture shall be withheld, as also the additional share of property due to the eldest; the additional share due to him as the eldest shall be obtained by his younger brother, who is superior to him in quality.

11.s: prāyaścitte tu carite pūrṇakumbhamapāṃ navam tenaiva sārdhaṃ prāsyeyuḥ snātvā puṇye jalāśaye
11.d: प्रायश्चित्ते तु चरिते पूर्णकुम्भमपां नवम् तेनैव सार्धं प्रास्येयुः स्नात्वा पुण्ये जलाशये
11.e: If however the expiation has been performed, they shall bathe with him in a sacred reservoir of water and shall throw into the water a fresh jar filled with water.

11.s: sa tvapsu taṃ ghaṭaṃ prāsya praviśya bhavanaṃ svakam sarvāṇi jñātikāryāṇi yathāpūrvaṃ samācaret
11.d: स त्वप्सु तं घटं प्रास्य प्रविश्य भवनं स्वकम् सर्वाणि ज्ञातिकार्याणि यथापूर्वं समाचरेत्
11.e: Having thrown that jar into the water, he shall enter his own house and carry on, as before, all his family-functions.

11.s: etadeva vidhiṃ kuryādyoṣitsu patitāsvapi etameva vidhiṃ vastrānnapānaṃ deyaṃ tu vaseyuśca gṛhāntike
11.d: एतदेव विधिं कुर्याद्योषित्सु पतितास्वपि एतमेव विधिं वस्त्रान्नपानं देयं तु वसेयुश्च गृहान्तिके
11.e: This same method is to be adopted also in the case of female outcasts; but clothing, food and drink shall be supplied to them and they shall live close to the house.

11.s: enasvibhiranirṇiktairnārthaṃ kiṃ cit sahācaret kṛtanirṇejanāṃścaiva na jugupseta karhi cit kṛtanirṇejanāṃścaitān
11.d: एनस्विभिरनिर्णिक्तैर्नार्थं किं चित् सहाचरेत् कृतनिर्णेजनांश्चैव न जुगुप्सेत कर्हि चित् कृतनिर्णेजनांश्चैतान्
11.e: One shall not carry on any business with unexpiated sinners; but in no case shall he despise those who have performed the expiation.

11.s: bālaghnāṃśca kṛtaghnāṃśca viśuddhānapi dharmataḥ śaraṇāgatahantr̥̄ṃśca strīhantr̥̄ṃśca na saṃvaset
11.d: बालघ्नांश्च कृतघ्नांश्च विशुद्धानपि धर्मतः शरणागतहन्त्र्̥̄ंश्च स्त्रीहन्त्र्̥̄ंश्च न संवसेत्
11.e: One shall not associate with murderers of children, ungrateful men, murderers of a refugee, and murderers of women,—even though they may have been duly purified.

11.s: yeṣāṃ dvijānāṃ sāvitrī nānūcyeta yathāvidhi tāṃścārayitvā trīn kṛcchrān yathāvidhyopanāyayet
11.d: येषां द्विजानां सावित्री नानूच्येत यथाविधि तांश्चारयित्वा त्रीन् कृच्छ्रान् यथाविध्योपनाययेत्
11.e: Though twice-born men to whom theSāvitrīhas not been taught according to rule, should be made to perform threeKṛcchrapenances and then initiated in due form.

11.s: prāyaścittaṃ cikīrṣanti vikarmasthāstu ye dvijāḥ brahmaṇā ca parityaktāsteṣāmapyetadādiśet
11.d: प्रायश्चित्तं चिकीर्षन्ति विकर्मस्थास्तु ये द्विजाः ब्रह्मणा च परित्यक्तास्तेषामप्येतदादिशेत्
11.e: When twice-born men, who follow improper occupations, or who are abandoned by the Veda, are desirous of performing expiations—for these also this same expiation is to be prescribed.

11.s: yadgarhitenārjayanti karmaṇā brāhmaṇā dhanam tasyautsargeṇa śudhyanti japyena tapasaiva ca
11.d: यद्गर्हितेनार्जयन्ति कर्मणा ब्राह्मणा धनम् तस्यौत्सर्गेण शुध्यन्ति जप्येन तपसैव च
11.e: WhenBrāhmaṇasacquire property by an objectionable act, they become pure by giving it up, and also by repeating sacred texts and performing austerities.

11.s: japitvā trīṇi sāvitryāḥ sahasrāṇi samāhitaḥ māsaṃ goṣṭhe payaḥ pītvā mucyate 'satpratigrahāt
11.d: जपित्वा त्रीणि सावित्र्याः सहस्राणि समाहितः मासं गोष्ठे पयः पीत्वा मुच्यते ऽसत्प्रतिग्रहात्
11.e: Having, with concentrated mind, repeated theSāvitrīthree thousand times, and drinking milk in a cow-pen for one month, he becomes absolved from the sin of accepting an improper gift.

11.s: upavāsakṛśaṃ taṃ tu govrajāt punarāgatam praṇataṃ prati pṛccheyuḥ sāmyaṃ saumyaicchasīti kim
11.d: उपवासकृशं तं तु गोव्रजात् पुनरागतम् प्रणतं प्रति पृच्छेयुः साम्यं सौम्यैच्छसीति किम्
11.e: When he has returned from the cow-pen, emaciated with the fast, and humble, they shall ask him—‘friend, dost thou desire equality with us?’

11.s: satyamuktvā tu vipreṣu vikiredyavasaṃ gavām gobhiḥ pravartite tīrthe kuryustasya parigraham
11.d: सत्यमुक्त्वा तु विप्रेषु विकिरेद्यवसं गवाम् गोभिः प्रवर्तिते तीर्थे कुर्युस्तस्य परिग्रहम्
11.e: Having said ‘Forsooth’ to theBrāhmaṇas, he shall scatter grass to the cows; whereupon they shall accord admission to him at a place hallowed by the cows.

11.s: vrātyānāṃ yājanaṃ kṛtvā pareṣāmantyakarma ca abhicāramahīnaṃ ca tribhiḥ kṛcchrairvyapohati
11.d: व्रात्यानां याजनं कृत्वा परेषामन्त्यकर्म च अभिचारमहीनं च त्रिभिः कृच्छ्रैर्व्यपोहति
11.e: If one sacrifices for apostates, or performs the obsequies of strangers, or malevolent rites, or theAhīnasacrifice,—he wipes it off by threeKṛcchras.

11.s: śaraṇāgataṃ parityajya vedaṃ viplāvya ca dvijaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ yavāhārastat pāpamapasedhati
11.d: शरणागतं परित्यज्य वेदं विप्लाव्य च द्विजः संवत्सरं यवाहारस्तत् पापमपसेधति
11.e: If a twice-born man has abandoned a refugee, or has tampered with the Veda, he atones for that offence by living upon barley for one year.

11.s: śvaśṛgālakharairdaṣṭo grāmyaiḥ kravyādbhireva ca narāśvauṣṭravarāhaiśca prāṇāyāmena śudhyati
11.d: श्वशृगालखरैर्दष्टो ग्राम्यैः क्रव्याद्भिरेव च नराश्वौष्ट्रवराहैश्च प्राणायामेन शुध्यति
11.e: When bitten by a dog, or a jackal, or an ass, or by a tame carnivorous animal, or by a man, or a camel, or a pig—he becomes pure by ‘breath-suppression.’

11.s: ṣaṣṭhānnakālatā māsaṃ saṃhitājapa eva vā homāśca sakalā nityamapāṅktyānāṃ viśodhanam omāśca śākalā
11.d: षष्ठान्नकालता मासं संहिताजप एव वा होमाश्च सकला नित्यमपाङ्क्त्यानां विशोधनम् ओमाश्च शाकला
11.e: For persons excommunicated from repasts, the purification consists in (a) eating at the sixth meal-time, reciting the Vedic text, and the daily offering of the ‘Sākala homa,’ for a month.

11.s: uṣṭrayānaṃ samāruhya kharayānaṃ tu kāmataḥ snātvā tu vipro digvāsāḥ prāṇāyāmena śudhyati
11.d: उष्ट्रयानं समारुह्य खरयानं तु कामतः स्नात्वा तु विप्रो दिग्वासाः प्राणायामेन शुध्यति
11.e: If aBrāhmaṇaintentionally hides a conveyance drawn by a camel, or one drawn by asses,—or if he bathes naked,—he becomes pure by ‘breath-suppression.’

11.s: vinā 'dbhirapsu vā 'pyārtaḥ śārīraṃ saṃniṣevya ca sacailo bahirāplutya gāmālabhya viśudhyati
11.d: विना ऽद्भिरप्सु वा ऽप्यार्तः शारीरं संनिषेव्य च सचैलो बहिराप्लुत्य गामालभ्य विशुध्यति
11.e: If, on being pressed, one passes bodily refuse, either without water, or in water, he becomes pure by bathing in his clothes, outside and touching a cow.

11.s: vedauditānāṃ nityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ samatikrame snātakavratalope ca prāyaścittamabhojanam
11.d: वेदौदितानां नित्यानां कर्मणां समतिक्रमे स्नातकव्रतलोपे च प्रायश्चित्तमभोजनम्
11.e: For the neglect of the compulsory duties laid down by the Veda, and for the omission of the observances of the Accomplished Student,—the expiation is fasting.

11.s: huṅkāraṃ brāhmaṇasyauktvā tvaṅkāraṃ ca garīyasaḥ snātvā 'naśnannahaḥ śeṣamabhivādya prasādayet
11.d: हुङ्कारं ब्राह्मणस्यौक्त्वा त्वङ्कारं च गरीयसः स्नात्वा ऽनश्नन्नहः शेषमभिवाद्य प्रसादयेत्
11.e: If a man has uttered the syllable ‘hum’ against aBrāhmaṇa, or has addressed a superior person as ‘thou,’—he shall bathe, fast for the rest of the day and having saluted him, shall propitiate him.

11.s: tāḍayitvā tṛṇenāpi kaṇṭhe vā 'badhya vāsasā vivāde vā vinirjitya praṇipatya prasādayet
11.d: ताडयित्वा तृणेनापि कण्ठे वा ऽबध्य वाससा विवादे वा विनिर्जित्य प्रणिपत्य प्रसादयेत्
11.e: Having struck him even with a blade of grass, or having tied him in the neck with a cloth, or having defeated him in an altercation,—one shall bow to him and appease him.

11.s: avagūrya tvabdaśataṃ sahasramabhihatya ca jighāṃsayā brāhmaṇasya narakaṃ pratipadyate
11.d: अवगूर्य त्वब्दशतं सहस्रमभिहत्य च जिघांसया ब्राह्मणस्य नरकं प्रतिपद्यते
11.e: If, with the intention of injuring aBrāhmaṇa, one has threatened him, he shall remain in hell for a hundred years; and for one thousand years, if he has struck him.

11.s: śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūn saṅgṛhṇāti mahītale tāvantyabdasahasrāṇi tatkartā narake vaset narake vrajet
11.d: शोणितं यावतः पांसून् सङ्गृह्णाति महीतले तावन्त्यब्दसहस्राणि तत्कर्ता नरके वसेत् नरके व्रजेत्
11.e: As many particles of dust on the ground asBrāhmaṇa’sblood coagulates, for so many thousand years will the shedder (of that blood lie in hell.

11.s: avagūrya caret kṛcchramatikṛcchraṃ nipātane kṛcchrātikṛcchrau kurvīta viprasyautpādya śoṇitam
11.d: अवगूर्य चरेत् कृच्छ्रमतिकृच्छ्रं निपातने कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रौ कुर्वीत विप्रस्यौत्पाद्य शोणितम्
11.e: On threatening aBrāhmaṇa, one shall perform theKṛcchra; on striking him, theAtikṛcchara, and on shedding his blood, both theKṛcchraand theAtikṛcchra.

11.s: anuktaniṣkṛtīnāṃ tu pāpānāmapanuttaye śaktiṃ cāvekṣya pāpaṃ ca prāyaścittaṃ prakalpayet
11.d: अनुक्तनिष्कृतीनां तु पापानामपनुत्तये शक्तिं चावेक्ष्य पापं च प्रायश्चित्तं प्रकल्पयेत्
11.e: For the atonement of offences for which no expiation has been prescribed, one should fix an expiation after taking into consideration the man’s capacity and the nature of the offence.

11.s: yairabhyupāyairenāṃsi mānavo vyapakarṣati tān vo 'bhyupāyān vakṣyāmi devaṛṣipitṛsevitān
11.d: यैरभ्युपायैरेनांसि मानवो व्यपकर्षति तान् वो ऽभ्युपायान् वक्ष्यामि देवऋषिपितृसेवितान्
11.e: I am now going to describe to you those methods, adopted by gods and sages andPitṛs, by means of which a man may wipe off his sins.

11.s: tryahaṃ prātastryahaṃ sāyaṃ tryahamadyādayācitam tryahaṃ paraṃ ca nāśnīyāt prājāpatyaṃ caran dvijaḥ
11.d: त्र्यहं प्रातस्त्र्यहं सायं त्र्यहमद्यादयाचितम् त्र्यहं परं च नाश्नीयात् प्राजापत्यं चरन् द्विजः
11.e: The twice-born, who is performing thePrājāpatya, shall eat in the morning for three days, then in the evening for three days, then for three days food got unasked, and for the next three days he shall not eat.

11.s: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśaudakam ekarātraupavāsaśca kṛcchraṃ sāṃtapanaṃ smṛtam
11.d: गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशौदकम् एकरात्रौपवासश्च कृच्छ्रं सांतपनं स्मृतम्
