11.e: Taking cow’s urine, cow-dung, milk, curds, clarified butter, kuśa-water, and fasting for one day,—has been declared to be ‘Sāntapana Kṛcchra’

11.s: ekaikaṃ grāsamaśnīyāt tryahāṇi trīṇi pūrvavat tryahaṃ caupavasedantyamatikṛcchraṃ caran dvijaḥ
11.d: एकैकं ग्रासमश्नीयात् त्र्यहाणि त्रीणि पूर्ववत् त्र्यहं चौपवसेदन्त्यमतिकृच्छ्रं चरन् द्विजः
11.e: The twice-born man who is performing the ‘Atikṛcchra’ shall eat only one mouthful at each of the three times mentioned above, for three days,—and shall fast during the last three days.

11.s: taptakṛcchraṃ caran vipro jalakṣīraghṛtānilān pratitryahaṃ pibeduṣṇān sakṛtsnāyī samāhitaḥ
11.d: तप्तकृच्छ्रं चरन् विप्रो जलक्षीरघृतानिलान् प्रतित्र्यहं पिबेदुष्णान् सकृत्स्नायी समाहितः
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇawho is performing the ‘Tapta-Kṛcchra’ shall drink hot water, hot milk, hot clarified butter and hot air,—each for three days; bathing once and having his mind concentrated.

11.s: yatātmano 'pramattasya dvādaśāhamabhojanam parāko nāma kṛcchro 'yaṃ sarvapāpāpanodanaḥ
11.d: यतात्मनो ऽप्रमत्तस्य द्वादशाहमभोजनम् पराको नाम कृच्छ्रो ऽयं सर्वपापापनोदनः
11.e: If a man, self-controlled and guarded, fasts for twelve days,—this constitutes the ‘Kṛcchra’ name ‘Parāka’, which removes all sins.

11.s: ekaikaṃ hrāsayet piṇḍaṃ kṛṣṇe śukle ca vardhayet upaspṛśaṃstriṣavaṇametatcāṇḍrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam
11.d: एकैकं ह्रासयेत् पिण्डं कृष्णे शुक्ले च वर्धयेत् उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणमेतत्चाण्ड्रायणं स्मृतम्
11.e: If one reduces his food by one morsel daily during the dark half of the month, and increases it during the light half,—bathing at the three ‘extractions,’—it is what has been called the ‘Cāndrāyaṇa.’

11.s: etameva vidhiṃ kṛtsnamācaredyavamadhyame śuklapakṣādiniyataścaraṃścāndrāyaṇaṃ vratam
11.d: एतमेव विधिं कृत्स्नमाचरेद्यवमध्यमे शुक्लपक्षादिनियतश्चरंश्चान्द्रायणं व्रतम्
11.e: This same method shall be adopted in the ‘Yavamadhyama’ penance, but beginning it in the bright half of the month; and it is with a controlled mind that one should perform the ‘Cāndrāyaṇa’ penance.

11.s: aṣṭāvaṣṭau samaśnīyāt piṇḍān madhyaṃdine sthite niyatātmā haviṣyāśī yaticāndrāyaṇaṃ caran
11.d: अष्टावष्टौ समश्नीयात् पिण्डान् मध्यंदिने स्थिते नियतात्मा हविष्याशी यतिचान्द्रायणं चरन्
11.e: One who performs the ‘Yati-Cāndrāyaṇa’ shall eat daily at midday eight morsels, controlling himself and eating only ‘sacrificial food.’

11.s: caturaḥ prātaraśnīyāt piṇḍān vipraḥ samāhitaḥ caturo 'stamite sūrye śiśucāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam
11.d: चतुरः प्रातरश्नीयात् पिण्डान् विप्रः समाहितः चतुरो ऽस्तमिते सूर्ये शिशुचान्द्रायणं स्मृतम्
11.e: TheBrāhmaṇa, with concentrated mind, shall eat four morsels in the morning, and four when the sun has set this is called the ‘Śiśu-Cāndrāyaṇa.’

11.s: yathā kathaṃ cit piṇḍānāṃ tisro 'śītīḥ samāhitaḥ māsenāśnan haviṣyasya candrasyaiti salokatām
11.d: यथा कथं चित् पिण्डानां तिस्रो ऽशीतीः समाहितः मासेनाश्नन् हविष्यस्य चन्द्रस्यैति सलोकताम्
11.e: If a man, with concentrated mind, somehow eats thrice eighty morsels of ‘sacrificial food,’ during a month, he attains the regions of the Moon.

11.s: etadrudrāstathā 'dityā vasavaścācaran vratam sarvākuśalamokṣāya marutaśca maharṣibhiḥ
11.d: एतद्रुद्रास्तथा ऽदित्या वसवश्चाचरन् व्रतम् सर्वाकुशलमोक्षाय मरुतश्च महर्षिभिः
11.e: The Rudras,Ādityasand the Maruts, along with the Great Sages, have performed this penance, for deliverance from all evils.

11.s: mahāvyāhṛtibhirhomaḥ kartavyaḥ svayamanvaham ahiṃsā satyamakrodhamārjavaṃ ca samācaret
11.d: महाव्याहृतिभिर्होमः कर्तव्यः स्वयमन्वहम् अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधमार्जवं च समाचरेत्
11.e: Homa-offerings shall be made by the man himself everyday, with the ‘Mahāvyāhṛtis,’ and he should practise harmlessness, truthfulness, freedom from anger, and mercy.

11.s: trirahnastrirniśāyāṃ ca savāsā jalamāviśet strīśūdrapatitāṃścaiva nābhibhāṣeta karhi cit
11.d: त्रिरह्नस्त्रिर्निशायां च सवासा जलमाविशेत् स्त्रीशूद्रपतितांश्चैव नाभिभाषेत कर्हि चित्
11.e: Thrice in the day and thrice in the night shall he enter water along with his clothes; and he shall never converse with women,Śūdrasand outcasts.

11.s: sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharedaśakto 'dhaḥ śayīta vā brahmacārī vratī ca syādgurudevadvijārcakaḥ
11.d: स्थानासनाभ्यां विहरेदशक्तो ऽधः शयीत वा ब्रह्मचारी व्रती च स्याद्गुरुदेवद्विजार्चकः
11.e: He shall pass his time standing and sitting; or if he is unable to do so, he may lie down on the ground ; he shall remain chaste, firm in vows, worshipping his elders, gods andBrāhmaṇas.

11.s: sāvitrīṃ ca japennityaṃ pavitrāṇi ca śaktitaḥ sarveṣveva vrateṣvevaṃ prāyaścittārthamādṛtaḥ
11.d: सावित्रीं च जपेन्नित्यं पवित्राणि च शक्तितः सर्वेष्वेव व्रतेष्वेवं प्रायश्चित्तार्थमादृतः
11.e: He shall constantly repeat theSāvitrī, as also other purificatory texts, to the best of his ability. This shall be done with due care, in connection with all penances performed for the sake of expiation.

11.s: etairdvijātayaḥ śodhyā vratairāviṣkṛtenasaḥ anāviṣkṛtapāpāṃstu mantrairhomaiśca śodhayet
11.d: एतैर्द्विजातयः शोध्या व्रतैराविष्कृतेनसः अनाविष्कृतपापांस्तु मन्त्रैर्होमैश्च शोधयेत्
11.e: By means of these penances are those twice-born persons to be purified whose sins have become known; those whose sins have not become known, one shall purify by means of sacred texts and Homa-offerings.

11.s: khyāpanenānutāpena tapasā 'dhyayanena ca pāpakṛtmucyate pāpāt tathā dānena cāpadi
11.d: ख्यापनेनानुतापेन तपसा ऽध्ययनेन च पापकृत्मुच्यते पापात् तथा दानेन चापदि
11.e: By confession, by repentance, by austerity and by study is the sinner freed from sin; as also by gifts in cases of difficulty.

11.s: yathā yathā naro 'dharmaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā 'nubhāṣate tathā tathā tvacaivāhistenādharmeṇa mucyate
11.d: यथा यथा नरो ऽधर्मं स्वयं कृत्वा ऽनुभाषते तथा तथा त्वचैवाहिस्तेनाधर्मेण मुच्यते
11.e: As a man, having committed a misdeed, goes on proclaiming it himself, so does he become freed from that sin, as a snake from its slough.

11.s: yathā yathā manastasya duṣkṛtaṃ karma garhati tathā tathā śarīraṃ tat tenādharmeṇa mucyate
11.d: यथा यथा मनस्तस्य दुष्कृतं कर्म गर्हति तथा तथा शरीरं तत् तेनाधर्मेण मुच्यते
11.e: As his mind goes on loathing the evil deed, so is his body freed from that sin.

11.s: kṛtvā pāpaṃ hi saṃtapya tasmāt pāpāt pramucyate naivaṃ kuryāṃ punariti nivṛttyā pūyate tu saḥ
11.d: कृत्वा पापं हि संतप्य तस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते नैवं कुर्यां पुनरिति निवृत्त्या पूयते तु सः
11.e: After having committed, a sin, if one repents, he becomes freed from that sin; he becomes purified by the renunciation—‘I shall not do so again.’

11.s: evaṃ sañcintya manasā pretya karmaphalaudayam manovācmūrtibhirnityaṃ śubhaṃ karma samācaret
11.d: एवं सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा प्रेत्य कर्मफलौदयम् मनोवाच्मूर्तिभिर्नित्यं शुभं कर्म समाचरेत्
11.e: Having thus considered in his mind the results arising after death from his deeds, he should perform good acts, by his thought, speech and body.

11.s: ajñānādyadi vā jñānāt kṛtvā karma vigarhitam tasmādvimuktimanvicchan dvitīyaṃ na samācaret
11.d: अज्ञानाद्यदि वा ज्ञानात् कृत्वा कर्म विगर्हितम् तस्माद्विमुक्तिमन्विच्छन् द्वितीयं न समाचरेत्
11.e: Either intentionally or unintentionally, if one has done a reprehensible act, he must not do it a second time, if he seeks absolution from the former.

11.s: yasmin karmaṇyasya kṛte manasaḥ syādalāghavam tasmiṃstāvat tapaḥ kuryādyāvat tuṣṭikaraṃ bhavet
11.d: यस्मिन् कर्मण्यस्य कृते मनसः स्यादलाघवम् तस्मिंस्तावत् तपः कुर्याद्यावत् तुष्टिकरं भवेत्
11.e: If in regard to any act that has been committed, his mind be uneasy, he shall perform the penance prescribed for it until it brings peace to his mind.

11.s: tapomūlamidaṃ sarvaṃ daivamānuṣakaṃ sukham tapomadhyaṃ budhaiḥ proktaṃ tapo 'ntaṃ vedadarśibhiḥ
11.d: तपोमूलमिदं सर्वं दैवमानुषकं सुखम् तपोमध्यं बुधैः प्रोक्तं तपो ऽन्तं वेददर्शिभिः
11.e: All happiness among gods and men has been declared by the wise ones to whom the Veda was revealed to have austerity for its source, austerity for its middle and austerity for its end.

11.s: brāhmaṇasya tapo jñānaṃ tapaḥ kṣatrasya rakṣaṇam vaiśyasya tu tapo vārtā tapaḥ śūdrasya sevanam
11.d: ब्राह्मणस्य तपो ज्ञानं तपः क्षत्रस्य रक्षणम् वैश्यस्य तु तपो वार्ता तपः शूद्रस्य सेवनम्
11.e: The ‘austerity’ for theBrāhmaṇais ‘knowledge’; the ‘austerity’ for theKṣatriyais ‘protecting’; the ‘austerity’ for the Vaiśya is ‘agriculture’; and the ‘austertty’ for the Śūdra is ‘service.’

11.s: ṛṣayaḥ saṃyatātmānaḥ phalamūlānilāśanāḥ tapasaiva prapaśyanti trailokyaṃ sacarācaram
11.d: ऋषयः संयतात्मानः फलमूलानिलाशनाः तपसैव प्रपश्यन्ति त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्
11.e: It is by austerity alone that self-controlled sages, subsisting on fruits, roots and air, survey the three worlds, including all moveable and immoveable beings.

11.s: auṣadhānyagado vidyā daivī ca vividhā sthitiḥ tapasaiva prasidhyanti tapasteṣāṃ hi sādhanam
11.d: औषधान्यगदो विद्या दैवी च विविधा स्थितिः तपसैव प्रसिध्यन्ति तपस्तेषां हि साधनम्
11.e: Medicines, drugs, science and the various kinds of divine condition are acquired by austerity; as austerity is the means of their accomplishment.

11.s: yaddustaraṃ yaddurāpaṃ yaddurgaṃ yacca duṣkaram sarvaṃ tu tapasā sādhyaṃ tapo hi duratikramam sarvaṃ tat tapasā
11.d: यद्दुस्तरं यद्दुरापं यद्दुर्गं यच्च दुष्करम् सर्वं तु तपसा साध्यं तपो हि दुरतिक्रमम् सर्वं तत् तपसा
11.e: What is hard to traverse, what is hard to attain, what is hard to reach, and what is hard to do,—all this is accomplished by Austerity; as Austerity is irrepressible.

11.s: mahāpātakinaścaiva śeṣāścākāryakāriṇaḥ tapasaiva sutaptena mucyante kilbiṣāt tataḥ
11.d: महापातकिनश्चैव शेषाश्चाकार्यकारिणः तपसैव सुतप्तेन मुच्यन्ते किल्बिषात् ततः
11.e: Those who have committed heinous offences, as also those who have committed other misdeeds, become freed from their sins by means of austerities well-performed.

11.s: kītāścāhipataṅgāśca paśavaśca vayāṃsi ca sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni divaṃ yānti tapobalāt
11.d: कीताश्चाहिपतङ्गाश्च पशवश्च वयांसि च स्थावराणि च भूतानि दिवं यान्ति तपोबलात्
11.e: Insects, snakes, moths, animals and birds, as also immovable beings go to heaven by the force of austerities.

11.s: yat kiṃ cidenaḥ kurvanti manovācmūrtibhirjanāḥ manovāckarmabhir tat sarvaṃ nirdahantyāśu tapasaiva tapodhanāḥ
11.d: यत् किं चिदेनः कुर्वन्ति मनोवाच्मूर्तिभिर्जनाः मनोवाच्कर्मभिर् तत् सर्वं निर्दहन्त्याशु तपसैव तपोधनाः
11.e: Whatever sin people commit by thought, word or deed,—all that they speedily burn away, having Austerity as their sole wealth.

11.s: tapasaiva viśuddhasya brāhmaṇasya divokasaḥ ijyāśca pratigṛhṇanti kāmān saṃvardhayanti ca
11.d: तपसैव विशुद्धस्य ब्राह्मणस्य दिवोकसः इज्याश्च प्रतिगृह्णन्ति कामान् संवर्धयन्ति च
11.e: It is only when theBrāhmaṇahas been purified by Austerities that Heavenly Beings accept their sacrifices and advance their interests.

11.s: prajāpatiridaṃ śāstraṃ tapasaivāsṛjat prabhuḥ tathaiva vedān ṛṣayastapasā pratipedire
11.d: प्रजापतिरिदं शास्त्रं तपसैवासृजत् प्रभुः तथैव वेदान् ऋषयस्तपसा प्रतिपेदिरे
11.e: It was by means of Austerity that LordPrajāpatigave forth these ordinances; and it was by means of Austerity that the Sages obtained the Vedas.

11.s: ityetat tapaso devā mahābhāgyaṃ pracakṣate yadetat tapaso sarvasyāsya prapaśyantastapasaḥ puṇyamuttamam puṇyamudbhavaṃ
11.d: इत्येतत् तपसो देवा महाभाग्यं प्रचक्षते यदेतत् तपसो सर्वस्यास्य प्रपश्यन्तस्तपसः पुण्यमुत्तमम् पुण्यमुद्भवं
11.e: The gods, discerning that the holy origin of all this lies in austerity, thus proclaim the magnificence of Austerity.

11.s: vedābhyāso 'nvahaṃ śaktyā mahāyajñakriyā kṣamā nāśayantyāśu pāpāni mahāpātakajānyapi
11.d: वेदाभ्यासो ऽन्वहं शक्त्या महायज्ञक्रिया क्षमा नाशयन्त्याशु पापानि महापातकजान्यपि
11.e: The daily recitation of the Veda, to the best of one’s ability, the ‘Great Sacrifices,’ and ‘tolerance,’ quickly destroy all sins,—even those due to heinous offences.

11.s: yathaidhastejasā vahniḥ prāptaṃ nirdahati kṣaṇāt tathā jñānāgninā pāpaṃ sarvaṃ dahati vedavit
11.d: यथैधस्तेजसा वह्निः प्राप्तं निर्दहति क्षणात् तथा ज्ञानाग्निना पापं सर्वं दहति वेदवित्
11.e: Just as fire, in a moment, consumes with its heat the fuel placed upon it, so does the man learned in the Veda destroy all sins by the fire of knowledge.

11.s: ityetadenasāmuktaṃ prāyaścittaṃ yathāvidhi ata ūrdhvaṃ rahasyānāṃ prāyaścittaṃ nibodhata
11.d: इत्येतदेनसामुक्तं प्रायश्चित्तं यथाविधि अत ऊर्ध्वं रहस्यानां प्रायश्चित्तं निबोधत
11.e: The due expiation of sins has thus been described; listen after this to the expiation of secret sins.

11.s: savyāhṛtipraṇavakāḥ prāṇāyāmāstu ṣoḍaśa api bhrūṇahanaṃ māsāt punantyaharahaḥ kṛtāḥ
11.d: सव्याहृतिप्रणवकाः प्राणायामास्तु षोडश अपि भ्रूणहनं मासात् पुनन्त्यहरहः कृताः
11.e: Sixteen ‘Breath-Suppressions’ with theVyāhṛtisand thePraṇava, performed daily, purify, in a month, even the ‘murderer of the embryo’ (Brāhmaṇa).

11.s: kautsaṃ japtvā 'pa ityetadvasiṣṭhaṃ ca pratīty ṛcam māhitraṃ śuddhavatyaśca surāpo 'pi viśudhyati
11.d: कौत्सं जप्त्वा ऽप इत्येतद्वसिष्ठं च प्रतीत्य् ऋचम् माहित्रं शुद्धवत्यश्च सुरापो ऽपि विशुध्यति
11.e: Even a drinker of wine becomes pure if he recites the ‘Kautsa hymn,’ beginning with the term ‘Ap,’ or the ‘Vāsiṣṭhahymn,’ consisting of the triad of verses beginning with ‘Prati,’ or the ‘Māhitrahymn,’ or the ‘Śuddhavati verses.’

11.s: sakṛtjaptvā 'syavāmīyaṃ śivasaṅkalpameva ca apahṛtya suvarṇaṃ tu kṣaṇādbhavati nirmalaḥ
11.d: सकृत्जप्त्वा ऽस्यवामीयं शिवसङ्कल्पमेव च अपहृत्य सुवर्णं तु क्षणाद्भवति निर्मलः
11.e: Having stolen gold, one instantly becomes free from impurity, by reciting once the ‘Āsyavāmīyahymn’ and the ‘Śivasaṅkalpahymn.’

11.s: haviṣpāntīyamabhyasya na tamaṃ ha itīti ca japitvā pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ mucyate gurutalpagaḥ
11.d: हविष्पान्तीयमभ्यस्य न तमं ह इतीति च जपित्वा पौरुषं सूक्तं मुच्यते गुरुतल्पगः
11.e: The Violator of the Preceptor’s Bed becomes absolved by repeating the ‘HaviṣpāntīyaHymn,’ (Ṛgveda, 10.88.1), the verse beginning with ‘na tamam ha’ (Ṛgveda, 10.126) and that beginning with ‘iti’ (Ṛgveda, 10.119),—and by reciting the ‘Puruṣasūkta’ (Ṛgveda, 10.90.1)

11.s: enasāṃ sthūlasūkṣmāṇāṃ cikīrṣannapanodanam avaity ṛcaṃ japedabdaṃ yat kiṃ caidamitīti vā
11.d: एनसां स्थूलसूक्ष्माणां चिकीर्षन्नपनोदनम् अवैत्य् ऋचं जपेदब्दं यत् किं चैदमितीति वा

11.s: pratigṛhyāpratigrāhyaṃ bhuktvā cānnaṃ vigarhitam japaṃstaratsamandīyaṃ pūyate mānavastryahāt
11.d: प्रतिगृह्याप्रतिग्राह्यं भुक्त्वा चान्नं विगर्हितम् जपंस्तरत्समन्दीयं पूयते मानवस्त्र्यहात्
11.e: If a man has accepted a gift that should not be accepted, or has eaten reprehensible food, he becomes pure in three days, by repeating theTaratsamandīya’ verses.

11.s: somāraudraṃ tu bahvenāḥ māsamabhyasya śudhyati samāmabhyasya sravantyāmācaran snānamaryamṇāmiti ca tṛcam
11.d: सोमारौद्रं तु बह्वेनाः मासमभ्यस्य शुध्यति समामभ्यस्य स्रवन्त्यामाचरन् स्नानमर्यम्णामिति च तृचम्
11.e: One who has committed many sins becomes purified by reciting, for a year, the ‘Somāraudrahymn’ and the three verses beginning with ‘aryamaṇam,’—while taking his bath in a stream.

11.s: abdārdhamindramityetadenasvī saptakaṃ japet apraśastaṃ tu kṛtvā 'psu māsamāsīta bhaikṣabhuk
11.d: अब्दार्धमिन्द्रमित्येतदेनस्वी सप्तकं जपेत् अप्रशस्तं तु कृत्वा ऽप्सु मासमासीत भैक्षभुक्
11.e: An offender shall recite, for half the year, the seven verses beginning with ‘Indram’; but he who has committed a reprehensible act in water shall subsist, for one month, on alms.

11.s: mantraiḥ śākalahomīyairabdaṃ hutvā ghṛtaṃ dvijaḥ sugurvapyapahantyeno japtvā vā nama ity ṛcam
11.d: मन्त्रैः शाकलहोमीयैरब्दं हुत्वा घृतं द्विजः सुगुर्वप्यपहन्त्येनो जप्त्वा वा नम इत्य् ऋचम्
11.e: A twice-born person destroys even the most grievous sin by making Homa-offerings of clarified butter for one year, with the sacred texts related to the ‘Śākala-homa,’ or by repeating the verse beginning with ‘namaḥ.’

11.s: mahāpātakasaṃyukto 'nugacchedgāḥ samāhitaḥ abhyasyābdaṃ pāvamānīrbhaikṣāhāro viśudhyati
11.d: महापातकसंयुक्तो ऽनुगच्छेद्गाः समाहितः अभ्यस्याब्दं पावमानीर्भैक्षाहारो विशुध्यति
11.e: He who is polluted by a ‘heinous offence,’ should, with concentrated mind, attend upon cows; and by repeating thePāvamānīverses and subsisting on alms for one year, he becomes pure.

11.s: araṇye vā trirabhyasya prayato vedasaṃhitām mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ parākaiḥ śodhitastribhiḥ
11.d: अरण्ये वा त्रिरभ्यस्य प्रयतो वेदसंहिताम् मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैः पराकैः शोधितस्त्रिभिः
11.e: Or, if, purified by the performance of three ‘Parāka’ penances, and self-controlled, he repeats thrice the entire text of the Veda, in a forest, he becomes absolved from all sins.

11.s: tryahaṃ tūpavasedyuktastrirahno 'bhyupayannapaḥ mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaistrirjapitvā 'ghamarṣaṇam
11.d: त्र्यहं तूपवसेद्युक्तस्त्रिरह्नो ऽभ्युपयन्नपः मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैस्त्रिर्जपित्वा ऽघमर्षणम्
11.e: If a man fasts for, three days, and entering the water thrice a dat repeats the ‘AghamarṣaṇaHymn’ three times, he becomes absolved from all sins.

11.s: yathā 'śvamedhaḥ kraturājsarvapāpāpanodanaḥ tathā 'ghamarṣaṇaṃ sūktaṃ sarvapāpāpanodanam
11.d: यथा ऽश्वमेधः क्रतुराज्सर्वपापापनोदनः तथा ऽघमर्षणं सूक्तं सर्वपापापनोदनम्
11.e: Just as theAśvamedha, the king of sacrifices, is destructive of all sins, even so is the ‘AghamarṣaṇaHymn’ also destructive of all sins.

11.s: hatvā lokānapīmāṃstrīnaśnannapi yatastataḥ ṛgvedaṃ dhārayan vipro nainaḥ prāpnoti kiṃ cana
11.d: हत्वा लोकानपीमांस्त्रीनश्नन्नपि यतस्ततः ऋग्वेदं धारयन् विप्रो नैनः प्राप्नोति किं चन
11.e: Even if he kills the three worlds, or if he eats here and there, he does not incur any sin, if he retains theṚgveda(in memory).

11.s: ṛksaṃhitāṃ trirabhyasya yajuṣāṃ vā samāhitaḥ sāmnāṃ vā sarahasyānāṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
11.d: ऋक्संहितां त्रिरभ्यस्य यजुषां वा समाहितः साम्नां वा सरहस्यानां सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते
11.e: One becomes absolved from all sins by reciting, with concentrated mind, three times, the text of theṚkor of theYajuṣ, or of theSāman, along with the esoteric texts.

11.s: yathā mahāhradaṃ prāpya kṣiptaṃ loṣṭaṃ vinaśyati tathā duścaritaṃ sarvaṃ vede trivṛti majjati
11.d: यथा महाह्रदं प्राप्य क्षिप्तं लोष्टं विनश्यति तथा दुश्चरितं सर्वं वेदे त्रिवृति मज्जति
11.e: As a clod of earth, being thrown, becomes dissolved as soon as it gets into the water,—even so does all sin become engulfed in the threefold Veda.

11.s: ṛco yajūṃṣi cānyāni sāmāni vividhāni ca eṣa jñeyastrivṛdvedo yo vedainaṃ sa vedavit
11.d: ऋचो यजूंषि चान्यानि सामानि विविधानि च एष ज्ञेयस्त्रिवृद्वेदो यो वेदैनं स वेदवित्
11.e: TheṚk-verses, the primevalYajuṣ-texts, and the manifoldSāman-songs,—these constitute the ‘Threefold Veda’; he who knows this is ‘learned in the Vedas.’

12.s: ādyaṃ yat tryakṣaraṃ brahma trayī yasmin pratiṣṭhitā sa guhyo 'nyastrivṛdvedo yastaṃ veda sa vedavit
12.d: आद्यं यत् त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म त्रयी यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठिता स गुह्यो ऽन्यस्त्रिवृद्वेदो यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्

12.s: cāturvarṇyasya kṛtsno 'yamukto dharmastvayā 'naghaḥ karmaṇāṃ phalanirvṛttiṃ śaṃsa nastattvataḥ parām
12.d: चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य कृत्स्नो ऽयमुक्तो धर्मस्त्वया ऽनघः कर्मणां फलनिर्वृत्तिं शंस नस्तत्त्वतः पराम्
12.e: ‘O sinless one, the whole law for the four castes has been expounded by you; instruct us now in regard to the actual fruition of actions.’

12.s: sa tānuvāca dharmātmā maharṣīn mānavo bhṛguḥ asya sarvasya śṛṇuta karmayogasya nirṇayam
12.d: स तानुवाच धर्मात्मा महर्षीन् मानवो भृगुः अस्य सर्वस्य शृणुत कर्मयोगस्य निर्णयम्
12.e: The righteousBhṛgu, sprung for Manu, said to the Great Sages—‘Listen to the truth regarding the relation of Actions.’

12.s: śubhāśubhaphalaṃ karma manovācdehasaṃbhavam karmajā gatayo nr̥̄ṇāmuttamādhamamadhyamaḥ
12.d: शुभाशुभफलं कर्म मनोवाच्देहसंभवम् कर्मजा गतयो न्र्̥̄णामुत्तमाधममध्यमः
12.e: Actions proceeding from mind, speech and body are conducive to good and bad results; and the conditions of men, due to actions, are high, low and middling.

12.s: tasyaiha trividhasyāpi tryadhiṣṭhānasya dehinaḥ daśalakṣaṇayuktasya mano vidyāt pravartakam
12.d: तस्यैह त्रिविधस्यापि त्र्यधिष्ठानस्य देहिनः दशलक्षणयुक्तस्य मनो विद्यात् प्रवर्तकम्
12.e: Know the mind to be the instigator of all this that is connected with the body, and which is of three kinds, has three substrata and is endowed with ten distinct characteristics.

12.s: paradravyeṣvabhidhyānaṃ manasā 'niṣṭacintanam vitathābhiniveśaśca trividhaṃ karma mānasam
12.d: परद्रव्येष्वभिध्यानं मनसा ऽनिष्टचिन्तनम् वितथाभिनिवेशश्च त्रिविधं कर्म मानसम्
12.e: Coveting the wealth or others, scheming in one’s mind about what is undesirable, adhering to a wrong notion,—these are the three forms of ‘mental action.’

12.s: pāruṣyamanṛtaṃ caiva paiśunyaṃ cāpi sarvaśaḥ asaṃbaddhapralāpaśca vācmayaṃ syāccaturvidham
12.d: पारुष्यमनृतं चैव पैशुन्यं चापि सर्वशः असंबद्धप्रलापश्च वाच्मयं स्याच्चतुर्विधम्
12.e: Abusing, lying, calumniating all men, and idle prattling,—are the pour kinds of ‘verbal action.’

12.s: adattānāmupādānaṃ hiṃsā caivāvidhānataḥ paradāraupasevā ca śārīraṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam
12.d: अदत्तानामुपादानं हिंसा चैवाविधानतः परदारौपसेवा च शारीरं त्रिविधं स्मृतम्
12.e: Taking what has not been given, unsanctioned killing, and intercourse with the wives of others—these have been declared to be three kinds of ‘bodily action.’

12.s: mānasaṃ manasaivāyamupabhuṅkte śubhāśubham vācā vācā kṛtaṃ karma kāyenaiva ca kāyikam
12.d: मानसं मनसैवायमुपभुङ्क्ते शुभाशुभम् वाचा वाचा कृतं कर्म कायेनैव च कायिकम्
12.e: The good and the evil resulting from ‘mental acts,’ one experiences through the Mind alone; those of ‘verbal acts,’ through speech; and those of ‘bodily acts,’ through the body.

12.s: śarīrajaiḥ karmadoṣairyāti sthāvaratāṃ naraḥ vācikaiḥ pakṣimṛgatāṃ mānasairantyajātitām
12.d: शरीरजैः कर्मदोषैर्याति स्थावरतां नरः वाचिकैः पक्षिमृगतां मानसैरन्त्यजातिताम्
12.e: Through sinful acts due to the Body, man becomes inanimate; through those of Speech, a bird or a beast; and through those of Mind, he is born in the lowest caste.

12.s: vāgdaṇḍo 'tha manodaṇḍaḥ kāyadaṇḍastathaiva ca yasyaite nihitā buddhau tridaṇḍīiti sa ucyate
12.d: वाग्दण्डो ऽथ मनोदण्डः कायदण्डस्तथैव च यस्यैते निहिता बुद्धौ त्रिदण्डीइति स उच्यते
12.e: Control over Speech, control over the Mind and control over the Body,—the man in whose heart these are firmly fixed is called ‘the man of triple control.’

12.s: tridaṇḍametannikṣipya sarvabhūteṣu mānavaḥ kāmakrodhau tu saṃyamya tataḥ siddhiṃ niyacchati kāmakrodhau susaṃyamya tataḥ siddhiṃ nigacchati
12.d: त्रिदण्डमेतन्निक्षिप्य सर्वभूतेषु मानवः कामक्रोधौ तु संयम्य ततः सिद्धिं नियच्छति कामक्रोधौ सुसंयम्य ततः सिद्धिं निगच्छति
12.e: The man who keeps this ‘triple control’ in regard to all creatures, and rightly subdues desire and anger, thereby attains success.

12.s: yo 'syātmanaḥ kārayitā taṃ kṣetrajñaṃ pracakṣate yaḥ karoti tu karmāṇi sa bhūtātmaucyate budhaiḥ
12.d: यो ऽस्यात्मनः कारयिता तं क्षेत्रज्ञं प्रचक्षते यः करोति तु कर्माणि स भूतात्मौच्यते बुधैः
12.e: He who is the impeller of this body, him they call the ‘Kṣetrajña,’ ‘the Conscious Being’; while he who does the acts is called by the learned, the ‘Bhūtātman,’ ‘the Material Entity.’

12.s: jīvasaṃjño 'ntarātmā 'nyaḥ sahajaḥ sarvadehinām yena vedayate sarvaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca janmasu
12.d: जीवसंज्ञो ऽन्तरात्मा ऽन्यः सहजः सर्वदेहिनाम् येन वेदयते सर्वं सुखं दुःखं च जन्मसु
12.e: An inner ‘self,’ called ‘Jīva,’ ‘Soul,’ is different,—generated along with all embodied beings, through which one experiences pleasure and fain during the several births.

12.s: tāvubhau bhūtasaṃpṛktau mahān kṣetrajña eva ca uccāvaceṣu bhūteṣu sthitaṃ taṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhataḥ
12.d: तावुभौ भूतसंपृक्तौ महान् क्षेत्रज्ञ एव च उच्चावचेषु भूतेषु स्थितं तं व्याप्य तिष्ठतः
12.e: Both of these, the ‘Great Principle’ and the ‘Conscious Being,’ united with the material substances, subsist in Him who resides in all things, pervading them all.

12.s: asaṅkhyā mūrtayastasya niṣpatanti śarīrataḥ uccāvacāni bhūtāni satataṃ ceṣṭayanti yāḥ
12.d: असङ्ख्या मूर्तयस्तस्य निष्पतन्ति शरीरतः उच्चावचानि भूतानि सततं चेष्टयन्ति याः
12.e: From his body emanate innumerable forms, which constantly energise all kinds of beings.

12.s: pañcabhya eva mātrābhyaḥ pretya duṣkṛtināṃ nṛṇām pañcabhya eva bhūtebhyaḥ śarīraṃ yātanārthīyamanyadutpadyate dhruvam
12.d: पञ्चभ्य एव मात्राभ्यः प्रेत्य दुष्कृतिनां नृणाम् पञ्चभ्य एव भूतेभ्यः शरीरं यातनार्थीयमन्यदुत्पद्यते ध्रुवम्
12.e: In the case of misbehaved persons, there is produced out of five constituents, another strong body, for the suffering of torments, after death.

12.s: tenānubhūya tā yāmīḥ śarīreṇaiha yātanāḥ tāsveva bhūtamātrāsu pralīyante vibhāgaśaḥ
12.d: तेनानुभूय ता यामीः शरीरेणैह यातनाः तास्वेव भूतमात्रासु प्रलीयन्ते विभागशः
12.e: After they have suffered, through this body, the torments inflicted by yama, those constituents become dissolved into each of those same material elements.

12.s: so 'nubhūyāsukhaudarkān doṣān viṣayasaṅgajān vyapetakalmaṣo 'bhyeti tāvevaubhau mahaujasau
12.d: सो ऽनुभूयासुखौदर्कान् दोषान् विषयसङ्गजान् व्यपेतकल्मषो ऽभ्येति तावेवौभौ महौजसौ
12.e: Having suffered the evils produced by attachment to sensual objects, and conducive to misery, he, having his sins destroyed, approaches those same two glorious ones.

12.s: tau dharmaṃ paśyatastasya pāpaṃ cātandritau saha yābhyāṃ prāpnoti saṃpṛktaḥ pretyaiha ca sukhāsukham
12.d: तौ धर्मं पश्यतस्तस्य पापं चातन्द्रितौ सह याभ्यां प्राप्नोति संपृक्तः प्रेत्यैह च सुखासुखम्
12.e: Those two together carefully look into his merit and demerit, invested with which both, he obtains happiness or unhappiness, here and after death.

12.s: yadyācarati dharmaṃ sa prāyaśo 'dharmamalpaśaḥ yathācarati taireva cāvṛto bhūtaiḥ svarge sukhamupāśnute
12.d: यद्याचरति धर्मं स प्रायशो ऽधर्ममल्पशः यथाचरति तैरेव चावृतो भूतैः स्वर्गे सुखमुपाश्नुते
12.e: If he practises virtue for the most part, and vice only in a small degree, then, invested with those same material substances, he obtains happiness in heaven.

12.s: yadi tu prāyaśo 'dharmaṃ sevate dharmamalpaśaḥ tairbhūtaiḥ sa parityakto yāmīḥ prāpnoti yātanāḥ
12.d: यदि तु प्रायशो ऽधर्मं सेवते धर्ममल्पशः तैर्भूतैः स परित्यक्तो यामीः प्राप्नोति यातनाः
12.e: If on the other hand he practises vice for the most part, and virtue only in a small degree,—then, becoming deserted by those substances, he suffers the torments inflicted by Yama.

12.s: yāmīstā yātanāḥ prāpya sa jīvo vītakalmaṣaḥ tānyeva pañca bhūtāni punarapyeti bhāgaśaḥ
12.d: यामीस्ता यातनाः प्राप्य स जीवो वीतकल्मषः तान्येव पञ्च भूतानि पुनरप्येति भागशः
12.e: That personality, having suffered those torments inflicted by Yama, and thereby freed from sin, again enters into those very material substances, each in due proportion.

12.s: etā dṛṣṭvā 'sya jīvasya gatīḥ svenaiva cetasā dharmato 'dharmataścaiva dharme dadhyāt sadā manaḥ
12.d: एता दृष्ट्वा ऽस्य जीवस्य गतीः स्वेनैव चेतसा धर्मतो ऽधर्मतश्चैव धर्मे दध्यात् सदा मनः
12.e: Having recognised, in his own mind, the conditions of the Personality, due to Virtue and Vice, one should fix his heart upon Virtue.

12.s: sattvaṃ rajastamascaiva trīn vidyādātmano guṇān yairvyāpyaimān sthito bhāvān mahān sarvānaśeṣataḥ
12.d: सत्त्वं रजस्तमस्चैव त्रीन् विद्यादात्मनो गुणान् यैर्व्याप्यैमान् स्थितो भावान् महान् सर्वानशेषतः
12.e: Know Sattva, Rajas and Tamas to be the three qualities of the Self, by means of which the Great One completely pervades all these beings.

12.s: yo yadaiṣāṃ guṇo dehe sākalyenātiricyate sa tadā tadguṇaprāyaṃ taṃ karoti śarīriṇam
12.d: यो यदैषां गुणो देहे साकल्येनातिरिच्यते स तदा तद्गुणप्रायं तं करोति शरीरिणम्
12.e: Whichsoever of these qualities wholly predominates in a body, it makes the owner of that body abound in that quality.

12.s: sattvaṃ jñānaṃ tamo 'jñānaṃ rāgadveṣau rajaḥ smṛtam etadvyāptimadeteṣāṃ sarvabhūtāśritaṃ vapuḥ
12.d: सत्त्वं ज्ञानं तमो ऽज्ञानं रागद्वेषौ रजः स्मृतम् एतद्व्याप्तिमदेतेषां सर्वभूताश्रितं वपुः
12.e: ‘Sattva’ has been declared to be Knowledge, ‘Tamas,’ to be Ignorance, and ‘Rajas,’ to be Love and Hate;—such is the nature of these, all-pervading and interpenetrating all beings.

12.s: tatra yat prītisaṃyuktaṃ kiṃ cidātmani lakṣayet praśāntamiva śuddhābhaṃ sattvaṃ tadupadhārayet
12.d: तत्र यत् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं किं चिदात्मनि लक्षयेत् प्रशान्तमिव शुद्धाभं सत्त्वं तदुपधारयेत्
12.e: Whenever one perceives in himself something full of bliss, calm and pure,—he should know it to be ‘Sattva.’

12.s: yat tu duḥkhasamāyuktamaprītikaramātmanaḥ tadrajo pratīpaṃ vidyāt satataṃ hāri dehinām artṛ
12.d: यत् तु दुःखसमायुक्तमप्रीतिकरमात्मनः तद्रजो प्रतीपं विद्यात् सततं हारि देहिनाम् अर्तृ
12.e: What is mixed with pain and brings unhappiness to the Soul,—know that to be ‘Rajas,’ imperceptible and constantly attracting embodied beings.

12.s: yat tu syān mohasaṃyuktamavyaktaṃ viṣayātmakam apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ tamastadupadhārayet
12.d: यत् तु स्यान् मोहसंयुक्तमव्यक्तं विषयात्मकम् अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधारयेत्
12.e: What is mixed with stupefaction, undiscernible, of the nature of sensual objects, incapable of being reasoned about and uncognisable,—one should recognise as ‘Tamas.’

12.s: trayāṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ guṇānāṃ yaḥ phalaudayaḥ agryo madhyo jaghanyaśca taṃ pravakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ
12.d: त्रयाणामपि चैतेषां गुणानां यः फलौदयः अग्र्यो मध्यो जघन्यश्च तं प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः
12.e: I am now going to fully describe the results,—good, middling and bad—proceeding from these three qualities.

12.s: vedābhyāsastapo jñānaṃ śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ dharmakriyā 'tmacintā ca sāttvikaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam
12.d: वेदाभ्यासस्तपो ज्ञानं शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः धर्मक्रिया ऽत्मचिन्ता च सात्त्विकं गुणलक्षणम्
12.e: Vedic study, austerity, knowledge, purity, control over the organs, practice of virtue and meditation on the Soul,—are the characteristics of the quality of ‘Sattva.’

12.s: ārambharucitā 'dhairyamasatkāryaparigrahaḥ viṣayaupasevā cājasraṃ rājasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam
12.d: आरम्भरुचिता ऽधैर्यमसत्कार्यपरिग्रहः विषयौपसेवा चाजस्रं राजसं गुणलक्षणम्
12.e: Proneness to undertake work, impatience, commission of improper acts, constant addiction to sensual objects are the characteristics of the quality of ‘Rajas.’

12.s: lobhaḥ svapno 'dhṛtiḥ krauryaṃ nāstikyaṃ bhinnavṛttitā yāciṣṇutā pramādaśca tāmasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam
12.d: लोभः स्वप्नो ऽधृतिः क्रौर्यं नास्तिक्यं भिन्नवृत्तिता याचिष्णुता प्रमादश्च तामसं गुणलक्षणम्
12.e: Avarice, drowsiness, irresolution, cruelty, disbelief, bad character, habit of begging, and inattentiveness are the characteristics of the quality of ‘Tamas.’

12.s: trayāṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ guṇānāṃ triṣu tiṣṭhatām idaṃ sāmāsikaṃ jñeyaṃ kramaśo guṇalakṣaṇam
12.d: त्रयाणामपि चैतेषां गुणानां त्रिषु तिष्ठताम् इदं सामासिकं ज्ञेयं क्रमशो गुणलक्षणम्
12.e: This should be understood to be in brief the characteristic of these three qualities in order, as they appear at the three times.

12.s: yat karma kṛtvā kurvaṃśca kariṣyaṃścaiva lajjati taj jñeyaṃ viduṣā sarvaṃ tāmasaṃ guṇalakṣaṇam
12.d: यत् कर्म कृत्वा कुर्वंश्च करिष्यंश्चैव लज्जति तज् ज्ञेयं विदुषा सर्वं तामसं गुणलक्षणम्
12.e: When, having done, or doing, or going to do a certain act, a man happen to feel ashamed,—every such act should be understood by the learned to be characterised by the quality of ‘Tamas.’

12.s: yenāsmin karmanā loke khyātimicchati puṣkalām na ca śocatyasaṃpattau tadvijñeyaṃ tu rājasam
12.d: येनास्मिन् कर्मना लोके ख्यातिमिच्छति पुष्कलाम् न च शोचत्यसंपत्तौ तद्विज्ञेयं तु राजसम्
12.e: When, by a certain act, the man desires great fame in this world, and does not mind failure—this should be understood to partake of the quality of ‘Rajas.’

12.s: yat sarveṇaicchati jñātuṃ yanna lajjati cācaran yena tuṣyati cātmā 'sya tat sattvaguṇalakṣaṇam
12.d: यत् सर्वेणैच्छति ज्ञातुं यन्न लज्जति चाचरन् येन तुष्यति चात्मा ऽस्य तत् सत्त्वगुणलक्षणम्
12.e: When, however, the act is one which he wishes to understand in all its details, by doing which he does not feel ashamed, and by which his heart feels satisfied,—it is characterised by the quality of ‘Sattva.’

12.s: tamaso lakṣaṇaṃ kāmo rajasastvartha ucyate sattvasya lakṣaṇaṃ dharmaḥ śraiṣṭhyameṣāṃ yathauttaram
12.d: तमसो लक्षणं कामो रजसस्त्वर्थ उच्यते सत्त्वस्य लक्षणं धर्मः श्रैष्ठ्यमेषां यथौत्तरम्
12.e: Pleasure is the distinguishing feature of ‘Tamas,’ ‘Wealth’ is described to be that of ‘Rajas,’ and ‘Spiritual Merit’ is the distinguishing feature of ‘Sattva,’—each succeeding one of these being superior to the preceding.

12.s: yena yastu guṇenaiṣāṃ saṃsarān pratipadyate yena yāṃstu tān samāsena vakṣyāmi sarvasyāsya yathākramam
12.d: येन यस्तु गुणेनैषां संसरान् प्रतिपद्यते येन यांस्तु तान् समासेन वक्ष्यामि सर्वस्यास्य यथाक्रमम्
12.e: I am now going to describe, briefly, in due order, those migratory states into which one falls through each quality from among these.

12.s: devatvaṃ sāttvikā yānti manuṣyatvaṃ ca rājasāḥ tiryaktvaṃ tāmasā nityamityeṣā trividhā gatiḥ
12.d: देवत्वं सात्त्विका यान्ति मनुष्यत्वं च राजसाः तिर्यक्त्वं तामसा नित्यमित्येषा त्रिविधा गतिः
12.e: Those partaking of ‘Sattva’ reach the state of the gods, those endowed with ‘Rajas,’ the state of men, and those characterised by ‘Tamas,’ the state of beasts; such is the threefold migratory state.

12.s: trividhā trividhaiṣā tu vijñeyā gauṇikī gatiḥ adhamā madhyamāgryā ca karmavidyāviśeṣataḥ
12.d: त्रिविधा त्रिविधैषा तु विज्ञेया गौणिकी गतिः अधमा मध्यमाग्र्या च कर्मविद्याविशेषतः
12.e: This threefold Migratory State due to the qualities should be understood to be again of three kinds each—high, low and middling, in accordance with the peculiar character of the act and knowledge of each man.

12.s: sthāvarāḥ kṛmikīṭāśca matsyāḥ sarpāḥ sakacchapāḥ paśavaśca mṛgāścaiva jaghanyā tāmasī gatiḥ
12.d: स्थावराः कृमिकीटाश्च मत्स्याः सर्पाः सकच्छपाः पशवश्च मृगाश्चैव जघन्या तामसी गतिः
12.e: Inanimate beings, worms, insects, fishes, snakes, tortoise, cattle and wild animals,—represent the lowest state due to the quality of ‘Tamas.’

12.s: hastinaśca turaṅgāśca śūdrā mlecchāśca garhitāḥ siṃhā vyāghrā varāhāśca madhyamā tāmasī gatiḥ
12.d: हस्तिनश्च तुरङ्गाश्च शूद्रा म्लेच्छाश्च गर्हिताः सिंहा व्याघ्रा वराहाश्च मध्यमा तामसी गतिः
12.e: Inanimate beings, worms, insects, fishes, snakes, tortoise, cattle and wild animals,—represent the lowest state due to the quality of ‘Tamas.’

12.s: cāraṇāśca suparṇāśca puruṣāścaiva dāmbhikāḥ rakṣāṃsi ca piśācāśca tāmasīṣūttamā gatiḥ
12.d: चारणाश्च सुपर्णाश्च पुरुषाश्चैव दाम्भिकाः रक्षांसि च पिशाचाश्च तामसीषूत्तमा गतिः
12.e: Inanimate beings, worms, insects, fishes, snakes, tortoise, cattle and wild animals,—represent the lowest state due to the quality of ‘Tamas.’

12.s: jhallā mallā naṭāścaiva puruṣāḥ śastravṛttayaḥ dyūtapānaprasaktāśca jaghanyā rājasī gatiḥ
12.d: झल्ला मल्ला नटाश्चैव पुरुषाः शस्त्रवृत्तयः द्यूतपानप्रसक्ताश्च जघन्या राजसी गतिः
12.e: Stick-fencers, wrestlers, actors, men subsisting by the use of weapons, those addicted to gambling and drinking,—represent the lowest state among those partaking of the quality of ‘Rajas.’

12.s: rājānaḥ kṣatriyāścaiva rājñāṃ caiva purohitāḥ vādayuddhapradhānāśca madhyamā rājasī gatiḥ
12.d: राजानः क्षत्रियाश्चैव राज्ञां चैव पुरोहिताः वादयुद्धप्रधानाश्च मध्यमा राजसी गतिः
12.e: Kings,Kṣatriyas, priests of kings, and leading wranglers and warriors represent the middling state among those partaking of ‘Rajas.’

12.s: gandharvā guhyakā yakṣā vibudhānucarāśca ye tathaivāpsarasaḥ sarvā rājasīṣūttamā gatiḥ
12.d: गन्धर्वा गुह्यका यक्षा विबुधानुचराश्च ये तथैवाप्सरसः सर्वा राजसीषूत्तमा गतिः
12.e: Gandharvas, Guhyakas, ‘Yakṣas,’ the attendants of the gods, and all the Apsaras, represent the high state among those partaking of ‘Rajas.’

12.s: tāpasā yatayo viprā ye ca vaimānikā gaṇāḥ nakṣatrāṇi ca daityāśca prathamā sāttvikī gatiḥ
12.d: तापसा यतयो विप्रा ये च वैमानिका गणाः नक्षत्राणि च दैत्याश्च प्रथमा सात्त्विकी गतिः
12.e: Ascetics and hermits,Brāhmaṇas, celestial beings, lunar asterisms, and Daityas represent the first state partaking of ‘Sattva.’

12.s: yajvāna ṛṣayo devā vedā jyotīṃṣi vatsarāḥ pitaraścaiva sādhyāśca dvitīyā sāttvikī gatiḥ
12.d: यज्वान ऋषयो देवा वेदा ज्योतींषि वत्सराः पितरश्चैव साध्याश्च द्वितीया सात्त्विकी गतिः
12.e: Sacrificers, sages, gods, vedas, luminaries, years,PitṛsandSādhyasrepresent the second state partaking of ‘Sattva.’

12.s: brahmā viśvasṛjo dharmo mahānavyaktameva ca uttamāṃ sāttvikīmetāṃ gatimāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ
12.d: ब्रह्मा विश्वसृजो धर्मो महानव्यक्तमेव च उत्तमां सात्त्विकीमेतां गतिमाहुर्मनीषिणः
12.e: Brahmā, creators of the universe, Dharma, the Great One, Unmanifest,—these the wise ones describe as representing the best state partaking of ‘Sattva.’

12.s: eṣa sarvaḥ samuddiṣṭastriprakārasya karmaṇaḥ triḥprakārasya trividhastrividhaḥ kṛtsnaḥ saṃsāraḥ sārvabhautikaḥ
12.d: एष सर्वः समुद्दिष्टस्त्रिप्रकारस्य कर्मणः त्रिःप्रकारस्य त्रिविधस्त्रिविधः कृत्स्नः संसारः सार्वभौतिकः
12.e: Thus has been described the entire thrice threefold migratory process pertaining to all beings, arising out of the three kinds of action.

12.s: indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena dharmasyāsevanena ca pāpān saṃyānti saṃsārānavidvāṃso narādhamāḥ
12.d: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन धर्मस्यासेवनेन च पापान् संयान्ति संसारानविद्वांसो नराधमाः
12.e: Foolish men of the lowest class go through the vilest migratory states, in consequence of being addicted to the senses and by not attending to duties.

12.s: yāṃ yāṃ yoniṃ tu jīvo 'yaṃ yena yenaiha karmaṇā kramaśo yāti loke 'smiṃstat tat sarvaṃ nibodhata
12.d: यां यां योनिं तु जीवो ऽयं येन येनैह कर्मणा क्रमशो याति लोके ऽस्मिंस्तत् तत् सर्वं निबोधत
12.e: Into what wombs the soul enters,—and in consequence of what acts,—listen to that, in due order.

12.s: bahūn varṣagaṇān ghorānnarakān prāpya tatkṣayāt saṃsārān pratipadyante mahāpātakinastvimān
12.d: बहून् वर्षगणान् घोरान्नरकान् प्राप्य तत्क्षयात् संसारान् प्रतिपद्यन्ते महापातकिनस्त्विमान्
12.e: Persons who have committed the heinous offences, having passed, during several years, through dreadful hells, reach, after the expiation thereof, the following migratory states.

12.s: śvasūkarakharauṣṭrāṇāṃ go 'jāvimṛgapakṣiṇām caṇḍālapukkasānāṃ ca brahmahā yoniṃ ṛcchati
12.d: श्वसूकरखरौष्ट्राणां गो ऽजाविमृगपक्षिणाम् चण्डालपुक्कसानां च ब्रह्महा योनिं ऋच्छति
12.e: He who kills aBrāhmaṇaenters the womb of a dog, a pig, an ass, a camel, a cow, a goat, a sheep, a deer or a bird, or that of aCaṇḍālaor a Pukkasa.

12.s: kṛmikīṭapataṅgānāṃ viṣbhujāṃ caiva pakṣiṇām hiṃsrāṇāṃ caiva sattvānāṃ surāpo brāhmaṇo vrajet
12.d: कृमिकीटपतङ्गानां विष्भुजां चैव पक्षिणाम् हिंस्राणां चैव सत्त्वानां सुरापो ब्राह्मणो व्रजेत्
12.e: TheBrāhmaṇawho drinks wine shall enter the womb of worms, insects, moths, of birds feeding on ordure, or of carnivorous animals.

12.s: lūtā 'hisaraṭānāṃ ca tiraścāṃ cāmbucāriṇām hiṃsrāṇāṃ ca piśācānāṃ steno vipraḥ sahasraśaḥ
12.d: लूता ऽहिसरटानां च तिरश्चां चाम्बुचारिणाम् हिंस्राणां च पिशाचानां स्तेनो विप्रः सहस्रशः
12.e: TheBrāhmaṇawho steals gold shall (enter) a thousand times into the womb of the spider, the snake, the lizard, of aquatic animals or of carnivorousPiśācas.

12.s: tṛṇagulmalatānāṃ ca kravyādāṃ daṃṣṭriṇāmapi krūrakarmakṛtāṃ caiva śataśo gurutalpagaḥ
12.d: तृणगुल्मलतानां च क्रव्यादां दंष्ट्रिणामपि क्रूरकर्मकृतां चैव शतशो गुरुतल्पगः
12.e: The violator of the Preceptor’s Bed is born hundreds of times as grasses, shrubs, creepers, as carnivorous and fanged animals, or as beings of cruel deeds.

12.s: hiṃsrā bhavanti kravyādāḥ kṛmayo 'medhyabhakṣiṇaḥ parasparādinaḥ stenāḥ pretyāntyastrīniṣeviṇaḥ
12.d: हिंस्रा भवन्ति क्रव्यादाः कृमयो ऽमेध्यभक्षिणः परस्परादिनः स्तेनाः प्रेत्यान्त्यस्त्रीनिषेविणः
12.e: Sanguinary persons become carnivorous animals; the eaters of impure food become worms; thieves become creatures consuming their own kind; and those having intercourse with women of the lowest caste become Pretas.

12.s: saṃyogaṃ patitairgatvā parasyaiva ca yoṣitam apahṛtya ca viprasvaṃ bhavati brahmarākṣasaḥ
12.d: संयोगं पतितैर्गत्वा परस्यैव च योषितम् अपहृत्य च विप्रस्वं भवति ब्रह्मराक्षसः
12.e: He who associates with outcasts, he who approaches the wife of another person, and he who has stolen the property of aBrāhmaṇa, become ‘Brahmarākṣasas.’

12.s: maṇimuktāpravālāni hṛtvā lobhena mānavaḥ vividhāṇi ca ratnāni jāyate hemakartṛṣu
12.d: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानि हृत्वा लोभेन मानवः विविधाणि च रत्नानि जायते हेमकर्तृषु
12.e: The man who, through greed, steals gems, pearls and corals, or the various kinds of precious articles, is born among ‘Hemakartṛs.’

12.s: dhānyaṃ hṛtvā bhavatyākhuḥ kāṃsyaṃ haṃso jalaṃ plavaḥ madhu daṃśaḥ payaḥ kāko rasaṃ śvā nakulo ghṛtam
12.d: धान्यं हृत्वा भवत्याखुः कांस्यं हंसो जलं प्लवः मधु दंशः पयः काको रसं श्वा नकुलो घृतम्
12.e: By stealing grains one becomes a rat; by stealing bronze, a Haṃsa; by stealing water, a Plava; by stealing honey, a gnat; by stealing milk, a crow; by stealing sweets, a dog; and by stealing clarified butter, an ichneumon.

12.s: māṃsaṃ gṛdhro vapāṃ madgustailaṃ tailapakaḥ khagaḥ cīrīvākastu lavaṇaṃ balākā śakunirdadhi
12.d: मांसं गृध्रो वपां मद्गुस्तैलं तैलपकः खगः चीरीवाकस्तु लवणं बलाका शकुनिर्दधि
12.e: For stealing meat, a vulture; for stealing fat, a cormorant; for stealing oil, a ‘Tailapāyika’ bird; for stealing salt, aCīrīvāka; and for stealing curds, a ‘Balākā’-bird.

12.s: kauśeyaṃ tittirirhṛtvā kṣaumaṃ hṛtvā tu darduraḥ kārpāsatāntavaṃ krauñco godhā gāṃ vāggudo guḍam
12.d: कौशेयं तित्तिरिर्हृत्वा क्षौमं हृत्वा तु दर्दुरः कार्पासतान्तवं क्रौञ्चो गोधा गां वाग्गुदो गुडम्
12.e: For stealing silk, a partridge; for stealing linen, a frog; for stealing cotton-cloth, a crane; for stealing a cow, an alligator; and for stealing molasses, a ‘Vāgguda’-bird.

12.s: chucchundariḥ śubhān gandhān patraśākaṃ tu barhiṇaḥ chucchundarīḥ śvāvit kṛtānnaṃ vividhamakṛtānnaṃ tu śalyakaḥ
12.d: छुच्छुन्दरिः शुभान् गन्धान् पत्रशाकं तु बर्हिणः छुच्छुन्दरीः श्वावित् कृतान्नं विविधमकृतान्नं तु शल्यकः
12.e: For stealing excellent perfumes, a musk-rat; for stealing vegetables with leaves, a peacock; for stealing cooked food of various kinds, aŚvāvit; and for stealing uncooked food a hedge-hog.

12.s: bako bhavati hṛtvā 'gniṃ gṛhakārī hyupaskaram raktāni hṛtvā vāsāṃsi jāyate jīvajīvakaḥ
12.d: बको भवति हृत्वा ऽग्निं गृहकारी ह्युपस्करम् रक्तानि हृत्वा वासांसि जायते जीवजीवकः
12.e: For stealing fire, a heron; for stealing utensils, a ‘Gṛhakāri’-bird; for stealing red clothes, one is born as a ‘Jīvajīvaka’-bird

12.s: vṛko mṛgaibhaṃ vyāghro 'śvaṃ phalamūlaṃ tu markaṭaḥ strīṃ ṛkṣaḥ stokako vāri yānānyuṣṭraḥ paśūnajaḥ
12.d: वृको मृगैभं व्याघ्रो ऽश्वं फलमूलं तु मर्कटः स्त्रीं ऋक्षः स्तोकको वारि यानान्युष्ट्रः पशूनजः
12.e: For stealing a deer or an elephant, a wolf; for stealing a horse, a tiger; for stealing fruits and roots, a monkey; for stealing a woman, a bear; for stealing water, a ‘Stokaka’-bird; for stealing conveyances, a camel; and for stealing cattle, a goat.

12.s: yadvā tadvā paradravyamapahṛtya balātnaraḥ avaśyaṃ yāti tiryaktvaṃ jagdhvā caivāhutaṃ haviḥ
12.d: यद्वा तद्वा परद्रव्यमपहृत्य बलात्नरः अवश्यं याति तिर्यक्त्वं जग्ध्वा चैवाहुतं हविः
12.e: For taking by force any kind of property belonging to another, and for eating a sacrificial material that has not been offered, one inevitably becomes an animal.

12.s: striyo 'pyetena kalpena hṛtvā doṣamavāpnuyuḥ eteṣāmeva jantūnāṃ bhāryātvamupayānti tāḥ
12.d: स्त्रियो ऽप्येतेन कल्पेन हृत्वा दोषमवाप्नुयुः एतेषामेव जन्तूनां भार्यात्वमुपयान्ति ताः
12.e: For stealing things, women also should incur guilt on this same principle; they become the female of those same creatures that have been named.

12.s: svebhyaḥ svebhyastu karmabhyaścyutā varṇā hyanāpadi pāpān saṃsṛtya saṃsārān preṣyatāṃ yānti śatruṣu yānti dasyuṣu
12.d: स्वेभ्यः स्वेभ्यस्तु कर्मभ्यश्च्युता वर्णा ह्यनापदि पापान् संसृत्य संसारान् प्रेष्यतां यान्ति शत्रुषु यान्ति दस्युषु
12.e: If men of the various castes deviate from their occupations, under normal conditions, they migrate into vile migratory states and become servants among robbers.

12.s: vāntāśyulkāmukhaḥ preto vipro dharmāt svakāccyutaḥ amedhyakuṇapāśī ca kṣatriyaḥ kaṭapūtanaḥ kūṭapūtanaḥ
12.d: वान्ताश्युल्कामुखः प्रेतो विप्रो धर्मात् स्वकाच्च्युतः अमेध्यकुणपाशी च क्षत्रियः कटपूतनः कूटपूतनः
12.e: TheBrāhmaṇafallen off from his own duty becomes a ‘fire-mouthed’Pretafeeding on vomitings; and theKṣatriyaa ‘foul-nosed’ Preta feeding on impure substances and dead bodies.

12.s: maitrākṣajyotikaḥ preto vaiśyo bhavati pūyabhuk maitrākṣijyotikaḥ cailāśakaśca bhavati śūdro dharmāt svakāccyutaḥ
12.d: मैत्राक्षज्योतिकः प्रेतो वैश्यो भवति पूयभुक् मैत्राक्षिज्योतिकः चैलाशकश्च भवति शूद्रो धर्मात् स्वकाच्च्युतः
12.e: The Vaiśya, fallen from his duty, becomes the ‘Maitrākṣajyotika’Pretafeeding on pus; and theŚūdrabecomes a ‘Cailāśaka’ Preta

12.s: yathā yathā niṣevante viṣayān viṣayātmakāḥ tathā tathā kuśalatā teṣāṃ teṣūpajāyate
12.d: यथा यथा निषेवन्ते विषयान् विषयात्मकाः तथा तथा कुशलता तेषां तेषूपजायते
12.e: In the proportion that sensually-inclined persons go on indulging in sensual pleasures, in that same proportion their ardour for them goes on increasing.

12.s: te 'bhyāsāt karmaṇāṃ teṣāṃ pāpānāmalpabuddhayaḥ saṃprāpnuvanti duḥkhāni tāsu tāsviha yoniṣu
12.d: ते ऽभ्यासात् कर्मणां तेषां पापानामल्पबुद्धयः संप्राप्नुवन्ति दुःखानि तासु तास्विह योनिषु
12.e: By the repetition of the said sinful acts, those men with shall understanding undergo sufferings in the various forms of existence in this world.

12.s: tāmisrādiṣu caugreṣu narakeṣu vivartanam asipatravanādīni bandhanachedanāni ca
12.d: तामिस्रादिषु चौग्रेषु नरकेषु विवर्तनम् असिपत्रवनादीनि बन्धनछेदनानि च
12.e: (They also suffer) being tossed about in theTāmisraand other dreadful hells, and being bound and mangled in the ‘forest with sword-leaved trees’ and other places.

12.s: vividhāścaiva saṃpīḍāḥ kākaulūkaiśca bhakṣaṇam karambhavālukātāpān kumbhīpākāṃśca dāruṇān
12.d: विविधाश्चैव संपीडाः काकौलूकैश्च भक्षणम् करम्भवालुकातापान् कुम्भीपाकांश्च दारुणान्
12.e: Also various forms of torments, being devoured by ravens and owls, tortures from morasses and scorching sand, and terrible boiling in jars.

12.s: saṃbhavāṃśca viyonīṣu duḥkhaprāyāsu nityaśaḥ śītātapābhighātāṃśca vividhāni bhayāni ca
12.d: संभवांश्च वियोनीषु दुःखप्रायासु नित्यशः शीतातपाभिघातांश्च विविधानि भयानि च
12.e: Constant births in low forms of life, abounding in misery, afflictions from heat and cold, and terrors of various kinds.

12.s: asakṛdgarbhavāseṣu vāsaṃ janma ca dāruṇam bandhanāni ca kāṣṭhāni parapreṣyatvameva ca kaṣṭāni
12.d: असकृद्गर्भवासेषु वासं जन्म च दारुणम् बन्धनानि च काष्ठानि परप्रेष्यत्वमेव च कष्टानि
12.e: Repeated lying in wombs, agonising births, painful bondages, and slavery to others.

12.s: bandhupriyaviyogāṃśca saṃvāsaṃ caiva durjanaiḥ dravyārjanaṃ ca nāśaṃ ca mitrāmitrasya cārjanam
12.d: बन्धुप्रियवियोगांश्च संवासं चैव दुर्जनैः द्रव्यार्जनं च नाशं च मित्रामित्रस्य चार्जनम्
12.e: Inevitable decrepitude, the pangs of sickness, various forms of afflictions and unconquerable death.

12.s: jarāṃ caivāpratīkārāṃ vyādhibhiścaupapīḍanam kleśāṃśca vividhāṃstāṃstān mṛtyumeva ca durjayam
12.d: जरां चैवाप्रतीकारां व्याधिभिश्चौपपीडनम् क्लेशांश्च विविधांस्तांस्तान् मृत्युमेव च दुर्जयम्
12.e: Inevitable decrepitude, the pangs of sickness, various forms of afflictions and unconquerable death.

12.s: yādṛśena tu bhāvena yadyat karma niṣevate tādṛśena śarīreṇa tat tat phalamupāśnute
12.d: यादृशेन तु भावेन यद्यत् कर्म निषेवते तादृशेन शरीरेण तत् तत् फलमुपाश्नुते
12.e: With whatever disposition a man performs an act, the fruit thereof he reaps with a body of that same quality.

12.s: eṣa sarvaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ karmaṇāṃ vaḥ phalaudayaḥ naiḥśreyasakaraṃ karma viprasyaidaṃ nibodhata
12.d: एष सर्वः समुद्दिष्टः कर्मणां वः फलौदयः नैःश्रेयसकरं कर्म विप्रस्यैदं निबोधत
12.e: Thus has been indicated to you the entire manner in which results proceed from actions; now learn that act which brings about the Highest Good of theBrāhmaṇa.

12.s: vedābhyāsastapo jñānamindriyāṇāṃ ca saṃyamaḥ ahiṃsā gurusevā ca niḥśreyasakaraṃ param
12.d: वेदाभ्यासस्तपो ज्ञानमिन्द्रियाणां च संयमः अहिंसा गुरुसेवा च निःश्रेयसकरं परम्
12.e: Vedic Study, Austerity, Knowledge, Control of the Senses, Harmlessness, Service of Elders,—are the best means of attaining the Highest Good.

12.s: sarveṣāmapi caiteṣāṃ śubhānāmiha karmaṇām kiṃ citśreyaskarataraṃ karmauktaṃ puruṣaṃ prati
12.d: सर्वेषामपि चैतेषां शुभानामिह कर्मणाम् किं चित्श्रेयस्करतरं कर्मौक्तं पुरुषं प्रति
12.e: [Answer]—Of all these, Knowledge of the Self has been declared to be the most efficacious; since it is the best of all sciences, as Immortality is attained by its means.

12.s: sarveṣāmapi caiteṣāmātmajñānaṃ paraṃ smṛtam taddhyagryaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ prāpyate hyamṛtaṃ tataḥ
12.d: सर्वेषामपि चैतेषामात्मज्ञानं परं स्मृतम् तद्ध्यग्र्यं सर्वविद्यानां प्राप्यते ह्यमृतं ततः
12.e: [Answer]—Of all these, Knowledge of the Self has been declared to be the most efficacious; since it is the best of all sciences, as Immortality is attained by its means.

12.s: ṣaṇṇāmeṣāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ pretya caiha ca śreyaskarataraṃ jñeyaṃ sarvadā karma vaidikam
12.d: षण्णामेषां तु सर्वेषां कर्मणां प्रेत्य चैह च श्रेयस्करतरं ज्ञेयं सर्वदा कर्म वैदिकम्
12.e: Among the six aforesaid actions, the performance of ‘Vedic Acts’ should be regarded as the most efficacious for bringing about happiness in this world and as well as after death.

12.s: vaidike karmayoge tu sarvāṇyetānyaśeṣataḥ antarbhavanti kramaśastasmiṃstasmin kriyāvidhau
12.d: वैदिके कर्मयोगे तु सर्वाण्येतान्यशेषतः अन्तर्भवन्ति क्रमशस्तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् क्रियाविधौ
12.e: All these are fully included, each in its turn, in a particular course of performance of the Vedic Act.

12.s: sukhābhyudayikaṃ caiva naiḥśreyasikameva ca pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttaṃ ca dvividhaṃ karma vaidikam
12.d: सुखाभ्युदयिकं चैव नैःश्रेयसिकमेव च प्रवृत्तं च निवृत्तं च द्विविधं कर्म वैदिकम्
12.e: The ‘Vedic Act’ is of two kinds—(a) the ‘active,’ which is conducive to happiness and prosperity, and (b) the ‘passive,’ which is conducive to the highest good.

12.s: iha cāmutra vā kāmyaṃ pravṛttaṃ karma kīrtyate niṣkāmaṃ jñātapūrvaṃ tu nivṛttamupadiśyate
12.d: इह चामुत्र वा काम्यं प्रवृत्तं कर्म कीर्त्यते निष्कामं ज्ञातपूर्वं तु निवृत्तमुपदिश्यते
12.e: That which is done with knowledge and brings about the fulfilment of desires either in this world, or in the next, is described as ‘active’; while that which is done with knowledge and without desires, is declared to be ‘passive.’

12.s: pravṛttaṃ karma saṃsevyaṃ devānāmeti sāmyatām nivṛttaṃ sevamānastu bhūtānyatyeti pañca vai
12.d: प्रवृत्तं कर्म संसेव्यं देवानामेति साम्यताम् निवृत्तं सेवमानस्तु भूतान्यत्येति पञ्च वै
12.e: He who devotes himself to the ‘active’ side, attains equality to the gods; while he who devotes himself to the ‘passive’ section, passes beyond the five material substances.

12.s: sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani samaṃ paśyannātmayājī svārājyamadhigacchati
12.d: सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि समं पश्यन्नात्मयाजी स्वाराज्यमधिगच्छति
12.e: He who perceives the Self in all beings, and all beings in the Self,—and sacrifices to the Self,—attains self-sovereignty.

12.s: yathauktānyapi karmāṇi parihāya dvijottamaḥ ātmajñāne śame ca syādvedābhyāse ca yatnavān
12.d: यथौक्तान्यपि कर्माणि परिहाय द्विजोत्तमः आत्मज्ञाने शमे च स्याद्वेदाभ्यासे च यत्नवान्
12.e: Having renounced even the said acts, theBrāhmaṇashall concentrate his effort on the knowledge of Self, on calmness and on the study of the Veda.

12.s: etaddhi janmasāphalyaṃ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ prāpyaitat kṛtakṛtyo hi dvijo bhavati nānyathā
12.d: एतद्धि जन्मसाफल्यं ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः प्राप्यैतत् कृतकृत्यो हि द्विजो भवति नान्यथा
12.e: This represents the fulfilment of the object of one’s existence, specially for theBrāhmaṇa; it is only when he has attained this, and not otherwise, that the twice-born man has accomplished his purpose.

12.s: pitṛdevamanuṣyāṇāṃ vedaścakṣuḥ sanātanam aśakyaṃ cāprameyaṃ ca vedaśāstramiti sthitiḥ
12.d: पितृदेवमनुष्याणां वेदश्चक्षुः सनातनम् अशक्यं चाप्रमेयं च वेदशास्त्रमिति स्थितिः
12.e: ForPitṛs, gods and men, the Veda is the eternal eye; the teaching of the Veda is beyond power and illimitable. Such is the settled fact.

12.s: yā vedabāhyāḥ smṛtayo yāśca kāśca kudṛṣṭayaḥ śrutayo sarvāstā niṣphalāḥ pretya tamoniṣṭhā hi tāḥ smṛtāḥ
12.d: या वेदबाह्याः स्मृतयो याश्च काश्च कुदृष्टयः श्रुतयो सर्वास्ता निष्फलाः प्रेत्य तमोनिष्ठा हि ताः स्मृताः
12.e: Those ‘revealed texts’ that are outside the Veda, as also all the false theories, are useless, even when carried to perfection; as they have been declared to be founded on ‘darkness.’

12.s: utpadyante cyavante ca yānyato 'nyāni kāni cit utpadyante vinaśyanti tānyarvākkālikatayā niṣphalānyanṛtāni ca
12.d: उत्पद्यन्ते च्यवन्ते च यान्यतो ऽन्यानि कानि चित् उत्पद्यन्ते विनश्यन्ति तान्यर्वाक्कालिकतया निष्फलान्यनृतानि च
12.e: Those other (doctrines) which spring up and perish are all worthless and false, being of modern growth.

12.s: cāturvarṇyaṃ trayo lokāścatvāraścāśramāḥ pṛthak bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca sarvaṃ vedāt prasidhyati bhūtaṃ bhavadbhaviṣyaṃ ca
12.d: चातुर्वर्ण्यं त्रयो लोकाश्चत्वारश्चाश्रमाः पृथक् भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च सर्वं वेदात् प्रसिध्यति भूतं भवद्भविष्यं च
12.e: The four castes, the three worlds, the four life-stages, the past, the present and the future are each learnt from the Veda.

12.s: śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaśca pañcamaḥ vedādeva prasūyante prasūtirguṇakarmataḥ
12.d: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धश्च पञ्चमः वेदादेव प्रसूयन्ते प्रसूतिर्गुणकर्मतः
12.e: Sound, touch, colour, taste, and odour as the fifth, proceed from the Veda; their production being due to the ‘secondary rites.’

12.s: bibharti sarvabhūtāni vedaśāstraṃ sanātanam tasmādetat paraṃ manye yatjantorasya sādhanam
12.d: बिभर्ति सर्वभूतानि वेदशास्त्रं सनातनम् तस्मादेतत् परं मन्ये यत्जन्तोरस्य साधनम्
12.e: The eternal lore of the Veda upholds all beings; f or th is reason I regard this as the best means of accomplishing the ends of every creature.

12.s: senāpatyaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca daṇḍanetṛtvameva ca saināpatyaṃ sarvalokādhipatyaṃ ca vedaśāstravidarhati
12.d: सेनापत्यं च राज्यं च दण्डनेतृत्वमेव च सैनापत्यं सर्वलोकाधिपत्यं च वेदशास्त्रविदर्हति
12.e: It is only one who knows the Vedic lore that deserves the command over armies, Kingly authority, the office of the adjudicator of punishments and sovereignty over all men.

12.s: yathā jātabalo vahnirdahatyārdrānapi drumān tathā dahati vedajñaḥ karmajaṃ doṣamātmanaḥ
12.d: यथा जातबलो वह्निर्दहत्यार्द्रानपि द्रुमान् तथा दहति वेदज्ञः कर्मजं दोषमात्मनः
12.e: Just as fire, having gained strength, burns even green trees, even so does the person knowing the Veda consume all the evil effects of his deeds.

12.s: vedaśāstrārthatattvajño yatra tatrāśrame vasan ihaiva loke tiṣṭhan sa brahmabhūyāya kalpate
12.d: वेदशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञो यत्र तत्राश्रमे वसन् इहैव लोके तिष्ठन् स ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते
12.e: In whatever life-stage he may be, the person who knows the true meaning of the Vedic Scriptures becomes fit for union with brahman, even while dwelling in this world.

12.s: ajñebhyo granthinaḥ śreṣṭhā granthibhyo dhāriṇo varāḥ dhāribhyo jñāninaḥ śreṣṭhā jñānibhyo vyavasāyinaḥ
12.d: अज्ञेभ्यो ग्रन्थिनः श्रेष्ठा ग्रन्थिभ्यो धारिणो वराः धारिभ्यो ज्ञानिनः श्रेष्ठा ज्ञानिभ्यो व्यवसायिनः
12.e: Better than ignoramuses are those who ‘read the books’; better than the ‘reader of books’ are those who ‘retain’ them; better than the ‘retainers’ are those who have ‘knowledge’; and better than those having ‘knowledge’ are those who act.

12.s: tapo vidyā ca viprasya niḥśreyasakaraṃ param tapasā kilbiṣaṃ hanti vidyayā 'mṛtamaśnute
12.d: तपो विद्या च विप्रस्य निःश्रेयसकरं परम् तपसा किल्बिषं हन्ति विद्यया ऽमृतमश्नुते
12.e: Austerity and knowledge are conducive to the Highest Good of theBrāhmaṇa; by Austerity he destroys sins and by Knowledge he attains immortality.

12.s: pratyakṣaṃ cānumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhā ''gamam trayaṃ suviditaṃ kāryaṃ dharmaśuddhimabhīpsatā
12.d: प्रत्यक्षं चानुमानं च शास्त्रं च विविधा 'ऽगमम् त्रयं सुविदितं कार्यं धर्मशुद्धिमभीप्सता
12.e: If one desires to obtain the correct knowledge of Dharma, he should become fully acquainted with these three:—Perception, Inference and the Scriptures of various traditions.

12.s: ārṣaṃ dharmaupadeśaṃ ca vedaśāstrāvirodhinā yastarkeṇānusaṃdhatte sa dharmaṃ veda naitaraḥ
12.d: आर्षं धर्मौपदेशं च वेदशास्त्राविरोधिना यस्तर्केणानुसंधत्ते स धर्मं वेद नैतरः
12.e: If a man explores, by ratiocination, the Vedic teaching regarding Dharma, he alone, and no other, understands Dharma.

12.s: naiḥśreyasamidaṃ karma yathauditamaśeṣataḥ mānavasyāsya śāstrasya rahasyamupadiśyate upadekṣyate
12.d: नैःश्रेयसमिदं कर्म यथौदितमशेषतः मानवस्यास्य शास्त्रस्य रहस्यमुपदिश्यते उपदेक्ष्यते
12.e: The act conducive to the Highest Good is as has been here fully declared. Now is going to be set forth the secret of the Teachings of Manu

12.s: anāmnāteṣu dharmeṣu kathaṃ syāditi cedbhavet yaṃ śiṣṭā brāhmaṇā brūyuḥ sa dharmaḥ syādaśaṅkitaḥ
12.d: अनाम्नातेषु धर्मेषु कथं स्यादिति चेद्भवेत् यं शिष्टा ब्राह्मणा ब्रूयुः स धर्मः स्यादशङ्कितः
12.e: If the question should arise—“How should it be in regard to those points upon which the laws have not been declared?”—[the answer is]—what the culturedBrāhmaṇasdeclare, that shall be the undoubted law.

12.s: dharmeṇādhigato yaistu vedaḥ saparibṛṃhaṇaḥ te śiṣṭā brāhmaṇā jñeyāḥ śrutipratyakṣahetavaḥ
12.d: धर्मेणाधिगतो यैस्तु वेदः सपरिबृंहणः ते शिष्टा ब्राह्मणा ज्ञेयाः श्रुतिप्रत्यक्षहेतवः
12.e: ThoseBrāhmaṇas, by whom the Veda, along with its supplements, has been learnt in the right manner, and who are guided directly by the revealed texts,—shall be regarded as ‘cultur ed.’

12.s: daśāvarā vā pariṣadyaṃ dharmaṃ parikalpayet try 'varā vā 'pi vṛttasthā taṃ dharmaṃ na vicālayet
12.d: दशावरा वा परिषद्यं धर्मं परिकल्पयेत् त्र्य् ऽवरा वा ऽपि वृत्तस्था तं धर्मं न विचालयेत्
12.e: When an assembly consisting of at least ten men,—or of at least three men firm in their duty,—declares a certain law, one should not seek to dispute it.

12.s: traividyo hetukastarkī nairukto dharmapāṭhakaḥ trayaścāśramiṇaḥ pūrve pariṣat syāddaśāvarā
12.d: त्रैविद्यो हेतुकस्तर्की नैरुक्तो धर्मपाठकः त्रयश्चाश्रमिणः पूर्वे परिषत् स्याद्दशावरा
12.e: A person learned in the three Vedas, a logician, an investigator, a person knowing the Nirukta, a lawyer and three men belonging to the first three life-stages, shall constitute the ‘Assembly’; which shall consist of at least ten members.

12.s: ṛgvedavidyajurvidca sāmavedavideva ca try 'varā pariṣadjñeyā dharmasaṃśayanirṇaye
12.d: ऋग्वेदविद्यजुर्विद्च सामवेदविदेव च त्र्य् ऽवरा परिषद्ज्ञेया धर्मसंशयनिर्णये
12.e: A person knowing theṚgveda, a person knowing the Yajurveda, and a person knowing theSāmaveda, shall be understood to form the assembly of at least three members, competent to decide doubtful points of law.

12.s: eko 'pi vedaviddharmaṃ yaṃ vyavasyeddvijottamaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ paro dharmo nājñānāmudito 'yutaiḥ
12.d: एको ऽपि वेदविद्धर्मं यं व्यवस्येद्द्विजोत्तमः स विज्ञेयः परो धर्मो नाज्ञानामुदितो ऽयुतैः
12.e: That which even a singleBrāhmaṇalearned in the Veda decides to be the law, shall be understood to be the highest law,—and not what is asserted by ten thousand ignoramuses.

12.s: avratānāmamantrāṇāṃ jātimātraupajīvinām sahasraśaḥ sametānāṃ pariṣattvaṃ na vidyate
12.d: अव्रतानाममन्त्राणां जातिमात्रौपजीविनाम् सहस्रशः समेतानां परिषत्त्वं न विद्यते
12.e: Even if thousands ofBrāhmaṇascome together,—who have not fulfilled their duties, who are ignorant of the sacred texts, who subsist merely by the name of their caste,—the character of the ‘Assembly’ cannot belong to them.

12.s: yaṃ vadanti tamobhūtā mūrkhā dharmamatadvidaḥ tatpāpaṃ śatadhā bhūtvā tadvaktr̥̄nanugacchati
12.d: यं वदन्ति तमोभूता मूर्खा धर्ममतद्विदः तत्पापं शतधा भूत्वा तद्वक्त्र्̥̄ननुगच्छति
12.e: When ignorant men, partaking of the quality of ‘Tamas,’ declare a certain act as right, without knowing what ‘right’ means,—the sin of that act falls hundred-fold upon those who propound it.

12.s: etadvo 'bhihitaṃ sarvaṃ niḥśreyasakaraṃ param asmādapracyuto vipraḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
12.d: एतद्वो ऽभिहितं सर्वं निःश्रेयसकरं परम् अस्मादप्रच्युतो विप्रः प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम्
12.e: All that is conducive to the Highest Good has been thus expounded to you; theBrāhmaṇawho has not deviated from this, attains the highest state.

12.s: evaṃ sa bhagavān devo lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā dharmasya paramaṃ guhyaṃ mamaidaṃ sarvamuktavān
12.d: एवं स भगवान् देवो लोकानां हितकाम्यया धर्मस्य परमं गुह्यं ममैदं सर्वमुक्तवान्
12.e: Thus has the blessed Lord explained to me, with a desire to benefit mankind, the highest secret of Dharma.

12.s: sarvamātmani saṃpaśyet satcāsatca samāhitaḥ sarvaṃ hyātmani saṃpaśyannādharme kurute manaḥ matiṃ
12.d: सर्वमात्मनि संपश्येत् सत्चासत्च समाहितः सर्वं ह्यात्मनि संपश्यन्नाधर्मे कुरुते मनः मतिं
12.e: With a concentrated mind, one should perceive in the Self all things, real as well as unreal. One who perceives all things in the Self never turns his mind towards wrong.

12.s: ātmaiva devatāḥ sarvāḥ sarvamātmanyavasthitam ātmā hi janayatyeṣāṃ karmayogaṃ śarīriṇām
12.d: आत्मैव देवताः सर्वाः सर्वमात्मन्यवस्थितम् आत्मा हि जनयत्येषां कर्मयोगं शरीरिणाम्
12.e: The Self alone is all the gods; everything subsists in the Self; it is the Self that brings about the connection of these embodied beings with actions.

12.s: khaṃ saṃniveśayet kheṣu ceṣṭanasparśane 'nilam paktidṛṣṭyoḥ paraṃ tejaḥ snehe 'po gāṃ ca mūrtiṣu
12.d: खं संनिवेशयेत् खेषु चेष्टनस्पर्शने ऽनिलम् पक्तिदृष्ट्योः परं तेजः स्नेहे ऽपो गां च मूर्तिषु
12.e: One should withdraw theĀkāśainto the ten cavities, the Wind into the organs of touch and movement, the best Light into the organs of digestion and vision, the Water into the fluids, and the Earth into the solid limbs.

12.s: manasīnduṃ diśaḥ śrotre krānte viṣṇuṃ bale haram vācyagniṃ mitramutsarge prajane ca prajāpatim
12.d: मनसीन्दुं दिशः श्रोत्रे क्रान्ते विष्णुं बले हरम् वाच्यग्निं मित्रमुत्सर्गे प्रजने च प्रजापतिम्
12.e: The Moon into the mind, Space into the ear,Viṣṇuinto movement, Hara into strength, Agni into speech, Mitra into the excretions, andPrajāpatiinto the generative organ.

12.s: praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣāmaṇīyāṃsamaṇorapi rukmābhaṃ svapnadhīgamyaṃ vidyāt taṃ puruṣaṃ param
12.d: प्रशासितारं सर्वेषामणीयांसमणोरपि रुक्माभं स्वप्नधीगम्यं विद्यात् तं पुरुषं परम्
12.e: The ruler of all, who is minuter than the minutest atom, bright like gold, amenable to dream-cognition,—him should one know as the HighestPuruṣa.

12.s: etameke vadantyagniṃ manumanye prajāpatim indrameke pare prāṇamapare brahma śāśvatam
12.d: एतमेके वदन्त्यग्निं मनुमन्ये प्रजापतिम् इन्द्रमेके परे प्राणमपरे ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्
12.e: This some people call ‘Agni’; others, ‘Manu-Prajāpati’; others, ‘Indra’; others, ‘Prāṇa’; and yet others, ‘the Eternal Brahman.’

12.s: eṣa sarvāṇi bhūtāni pañcabhirvyāpya mūrtibhiḥ janmavṛddhikṣayairnityaṃ saṃsārayati cakravat
12.d: एष सर्वाणि भूतानि पञ्चभिर्व्याप्य मूर्तिभिः जन्मवृद्धिक्षयैर्नित्यं संसारयति चक्रवत्
12.e: He it is who, interpenetrating all beings, with his five forms, makes them, revolve constantly like a wheel, through birth, growth and decay.

12.s: evaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūteṣu paśyatyātmānamātmanā sa sarvasamatāmetya brahmābhyeti paraṃ padam
12.d: एवं यः सर्वभूतेषु पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मना स सर्वसमतामेत्य ब्रह्माभ्येति परं पदम्
12.e: He who thus perceives the Self through the Self, in all beings, becomes equal towards all and attains the highest state, Brahman.

12.s: ityetan mānavaṃ śāstraṃ bhṛguproktaṃ paṭhan dvijaḥ bhavatyācāravānnityaṃ yathaiṣṭāṃ prāpnuyādgatim samāptaṃ mānavaṃ dharmaśāstram
12.d: इत्येतन् मानवं शास्त्रं भृगुप्रोक्तं पठन् द्विजः भवत्याचारवान्नित्यं यथैष्टां प्राप्नुयाद्गतिम् समाप्तं मानवं धर्मशास्त्रम्
12.e: The twice-born man who reads these Ordinances of Manu, shall be ever equipped with virtue and shall attain whatever state he may desire.
